aiTitle: vd4dot優化後activation Q8_0與weight計算方式

input.command: grep -n "q1_0x64_sign_bit" -A 40 ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.h | head -70
input.description: Show sign-bit layout helper

content: gemv 的kernel code 在哪裡?

content.text:
**Short answer:** the activation is not spread across the vector lanes. Four consecutive Q8_0 quants are packed into one 32-bit word and **broadcast to all 64 lanes**; the weights are what varies per lane. `nds.vd4dots.vv` then does one 4-way int8 dot per lane, so one instruction = 64 rows x 4 columns = 256 MACs.

## The instruction

```
nds.vd4dots.vv  vd, vs1, vs2      (e32, m2 -> 64 i32 lanes)
lane j:  vd[j] += sum_{t=0..3} vs1_i8[4j+t] * vs2_i8[4j+t]
```
Same register group, two views: 64 i32 lanes, or 256 i8 bytes.

## What goes into each operand

`repack.cpp:1889-1894`

| operand | content | how it is built |
|---|---|---|
| `vs1` = w | row j, columns c..c+3, as +1/-1 int8 | `vlm_v_b4` one 32-byte sign plane -> `vmerge(-1, +1)` |
| `vs2` = s | activation columns c..c+3, **same in every lane** | 4 int8 read as one `uint32` GPR -> `vmv.v.x` |
| `vd` = acc | per-row int32 partial sum | chained across quads |

The Q1_D4 repack order (`repack.h:157`) exists exactly for this: bit `(c/4)*256 + 4*j + (c%4)`, so the mask load lands row j's four columns in byte lanes `4j..4j+3` with no shuffle.

```
w   (i8 view): [r0c0 r0c1 r0c2 r0c3][r1c0 r1c1 r1c2 r1c3] ... [r63c0..c3]
s   (i8 view): [ a0   a1   a2   a3 ][ a0   a1   a2   a3 ] ... [ a0 .. a3 ]  <- broadcast
acc (i32):     [   row0 dot      ][    row1 dot      ] ... [  row63 dot  ]
```

## Loop and scales

`repack.cpp:1879-1899`

1. One Q8_0 group = 32 columns = 8 quads. Four quads per asm block, one `vsetvli` for all four dots (`q1_vd4dots_x4_m2`).
2. After the group: `acc` (int32) -> float, multiply by the **activation scale** `a_ptr[g].d`, add into `facc`.
3. After 4 groups (QK1_0=128): multiply by the **weight scale vector** `dx` (64 per-row fp16 scales, expanded with integer bit math) and add into `sumf`.

```
out[row] = sum_l  dx[l][row] * ( sum_k  da[g] * acc_int[g][row] )
```

## gemm difference

`repack.cpp:1938-1946, 1831-1851` - one weight vector is reused against **4 activation rows**: 4 broadcasts, 4 dots, 4 accumulators, weight stream read once per 4 rows. The `block_q8_0x4` interleaving (`qs[c*4 + m]`) is the wrong order for the dot, so the row tile is de-interleaved once up front with `vnsrl` (u32 -> u16 -> u8). Register pressure kills the per-block `facc`, so there the activation scale is folded into `dx` instead.

## Two traps baked into the code

- The broadcast must be hand-written `vmv.v.x`. Given the intrinsic, GCC contracts "load word + splat" into `vlse32.v vd,(rs1),zero`, which is element-serial on this core - 18x slower. Passing the quads as plain `uint32` GPRs makes that contraction impossible.
- gemv restages activations through byte ld/st into `aq` first (`repack.cpp:1864-1867`): `block_q8_0.qs` sits at struct offset 2, so every other group is 2 mod 4 and a 32-bit vector element load faults. `block_q8_0x4` is 4-byte aligned, so gemm skips this.

content.text:
Full chain, top to bottom:

| layer | location | role |
|---|---|---|
| ggml op | `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4209` | `forward_mul_mat` calls into the repack gemv |
| arch entry | `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:2159` `ggml_gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0` | VLEN dispatch, falls back to generic |
| **d4 kernel** | **`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1853` `q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024`** | the `nds.vd4dots.vv` one, needs `Q1_D4` + `vlenb >= 128` |
| dot helper | `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1809` `q1_vd4dots_x4_m2` | the inline asm block, 4 dots per `vsetvli` |
| plain RVV | `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:2026` / `:1998` | `vl1024` / `vl512`, used when `Q1_D4` is OFF |
| scalar ref | `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:3211` | `_generic`, correctness reference |

Note the dispatch is asymmetric: when `Q1_D4=1` there is **no** VLEN=512 path, so `vlenb < 128` drops straight to the generic scalar kernel (`:2164-2178`). That is intentional - e32/m2 only equals 64 lanes at VLEN>=1024.

The build switch is `-DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt`), which appends `_xandesvdot` to `-march` and defines `Q1_D4` for the whole cpu target, flipping both the kernel choice and the repack sign-plane order (`repack.h:157`) together.

message.content: 你的D4 是代表 vd4dot instruction?

content.text:
Yes. `D4` = the `d4` in `nds.vd4dots.vv` - "dot product, 4 elements at a time".

Where the name appears:

- `Q1_D4` - the build macro, set by `-DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON`. Q1_0 weights + the d4 dot.
- `q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024` / `q1_gemm_64d4_vl1024` - `64` = 64 rows per tile, `d4` = this dot, `vl1024` = needs VLEN >= 1024.
- `q1_vd4dots_x4_m2` - the asm helper. Here the `x4` means something different: 4 dot instructions per `vsetvli`, not the 4 elements.

The `4` is also why the repack layout changes. `nds.vd4dots.vv` makes each i32 lane consume 4 int8 bytes, so `q1_0x64_sign_bit` (`repack.h:157`) must put 4 columns of one row into 4 neighbouring bytes:

```
Q1_D4=0:  bit = c*64 + j              one plane = 1 column x 64 rows
Q1_D4=1:  bit = (c/4)*256 + 4*j + c%4 one plane = 4 columns x 64 rows
```

Same block size, same bytes, only the permutation differs. So `D4` names one decision that runs through the instruction, the kernel, and the data layout together.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Codegen gate for the Q1_D4 kernels (ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp).
#
# Two things this catches that no result test can:
#
#  1. A path silently falls back. Q1_D4 changes the sign-plane order AND the
#     kernel; if gemv or gemm never got a vd4dots kernel it still returns
#     correct numbers through the generic C path, just ~3x slower. Counting
#     nds.vd4dots is the only way to see which one is really on the

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 kernel A/Bs:
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   d4       = repack + prefetch + nds.vd4dots.vv kernels (XAndesVDot)
#   d4-nopf  = d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh d4                 # the vd4dots kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# Which MUL_MAT node the ROI brackets. Compile-time because andesim's linux
# runtime hands the guest an EMPTY envp (runtime/linux/stack.h), so the
# GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K env override never reaches the guest -- one binary per
# measured node. Bonsai-4B layer 7 shape table:
#   50 attn_q  51 attn_v  52 attn_k  53 attn_output  54 ffn_gate  55 ffn_up
#   56 ffn_down                                       253 result_output
# K=51 keeps the original unsuffixed artifact names; anything else appends -k<K>.
ROI_K=${ROI_K:-51}
SUF=""; [ "$ROI_K" = 51 ] || SUF="-k$ROI_K"

# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                  : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK        : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON      : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                              gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON  : single switch for the d4 kernels - appends _xandesvdot
#                              to -march AND defines Q1_D4 (kernels + sign-plane order)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N     : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack/vdot toggles   $3 extra defines (DIST etc., or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | d4 | d4-nopf | *-nodpref
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 = the shipped kernel with the K-reduction handed to nds.vd4dots.vv.
    # GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT is the whole switch: -march plus the Q1_D4 source gate
    # (kernels and sign-plane repack order), so no extra define is needed.
    d4)       cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF. Answers "is the d4 kernel still
    # memory-bound?" - if this lands near d4, the weight stream is fully hidden
    # and there is nothing left for a bigger/faster memory to recover.

#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   d4       = repack + prefetch + nds.vd4dots.vv kernels (XAndesVDot)
#   d4-nopf  = d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh d4                 # the vd4dots kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# Which MUL_MAT node the ROI brackets. Compile-time because andesim's linux
# runtime hands the guest an EMPTY envp (runtime/linux/stack.h), so the
# GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K env override never reaches the guest -- one binary per
# measured node. Bonsai-4B layer 7 shape table:
#   50 attn_q  51 attn_v  52 attn_k  53 attn_output  54 ffn_gate  55 ffn_up
#   56 ffn_down                                       253 result_output
# K=51 keeps the original unsuffixed artifact names; anything else appends -k<K>.
ROI_K=${ROI_K:-51}
SUF=""; [ "$ROI_K" = 51 ] || SUF="-k$ROI_K"

# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                  : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK        : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON      : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                              gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)

#                              to -march AND defines Q1_D4 (kernels + sign-plane order)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fast-mode whole-model check for q1_0_reproduce.md Level 3.
#
# Runs the three configurations that actually ship, under andesim --mode fast
# (QEMU only - functional, no cycle leg), greedy, same prompt, and compares
# each optimized build's generated text against upstream's:
#
#   pristine  GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF                      <- the reference
#   prefetch  repack + weight-stream prefetch (DIST=1)
#   d4        repack + prefetch + nds.vd4dots.vv
#
#   bash verify.sh                  # 4b model, prefetch and d4 vs pristine
#   MODEL=8b bash verify.sh         # same, on Bonsai-8B
#   MODEL=27b bash verify.sh
#   MODEL=/path/to/x.gguf bash verify.sh
#   REF=baseline bash verify.sh prefetch    # isolate the prefetch hint alone
#
# Why equality is the right bar, per comparison:
#
#   prefetch vs pristine  Expected to match exactly. Upstream's VLEN>=256 path
#       (ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0_vl256) reduces as `acc += d1*sumi` per q8 group
#       then `sumf += d0*acc` per block, and the repack gemv uses that same
#       nesting (facc per group, sumf per block). prefetch.r on top is an
#       architectural hint and cannot change a result, so a mismatch means the
#       repack layout or the prefetch helper's address math is wrong.
#
#   d4 vs pristine  Not guaranteed bit-for-bit. The gemv keeps the nesting
#       above, so decode is exact, but the d4 GEMM folds dx*ad[m] into each q8
#       group and accumulates into sumf 4x per block (q1_gemm_64d4_vl1024)
#       where the others build facc first and accumulate once per block. That
#       is a different rounding order, so PREFILL floats differ at the ULP
#       level by construction. Equal greedy text is the acceptance bar; if it
#       ever fails, compare tensors with a tolerance, do not hunt a logic bug.
#
# Minutes per binary. Override via env LLAMA / ANDESIM / MODEL / REF / PROMPT / NGEN.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
# --engine is NOT cosmetic in fast mode: it picks QEMU's -cpu and VLEN.
# vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 -> andes-ax46mpv,vlen=1024; omitting it falls back to
# andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, where q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024 does not apply and the d4
# build silently drops to the generic kernel - the comparison would still PASS
# while testing nothing. Keep this at a VLEN>=1024 engine.
ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
REF=${REF:-pristine}
PROMPT=${PROMPT:-The capital of France is}
NGEN=${NGEN:-16}

# Model selection. The bigger models need more guest RAM than the 4B, and need
# --no-mmap because the mapped file does not fit the guest window. These are
# FAST-mode sizes: unlike hybrid, fast mode has no 2G cap (it is just QEMU's
# -m), but QEMU takes whole MiB - the hybrid runbook's 2097148K is rejected here.
case "${MODEL:-4b}" in
  4b)  GGUF="$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf";  MEM=${MEM:-2000M}; MMAP="" ;;
  8b)  GGUF="$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf";  MEM=${MEM:-4G};    MMAP="--no-mmap" ;;
  27b) GGUF="$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf"; MEM=${MEM:-8G};    MMAP="--no-mmap" ;;
  *)   GGUF="$MODEL";                             MEM=${MEM:-8G};    MMAP="--no-mmap" ;;
esac
[ -f "$GGUF" ] || { echo "no such model: $GGUF" >&2; exit 1; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run a riscv64 llama.cpp binary under Andes QEMU (user-mode).
#
# Usage:   ./run-rv64-qemu.sh <binary-name-or-path> [args...]
# Example: ./run-rv64-qemu.sh llama-bench -m model.gguf -p 8 -n 4 -r 1 -t 1
#
# Overridable via environment:
#   ANDES_ROOT  Andes SW release root
#   QEMU        Andes linux-user qemu-riscv64
#   SYSROOT     toolchain glibc sysroot (matches the xandes-built libc)
#   BIN_DIR     directory with the cross-built binaries and libggml*/libllama* .so
#   QEMU_CPU    QEMU cpu string; zfh/zvfh must be enabled explicitly:
#               andes-ax45mpv does not enable them by default and
#               ggml_cpu_fp32_to_fp16 (vfncvt.f.f.w) SIGILLs without zvfh
#   MODEL       default model, added as "-m $MODEL" when no -m is given
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ANDES_ROOT=${ANDES_ROOT:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542}
QEMU=${QEMU:-$ANDES_ROOT/build-qemu/linux/qemu-riscv64}
SYSROOT=${SYSROOT:-$ANDES_ROOT/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d/sysroot}
BIN_DIR=${BIN_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/build-rv64/bin}
QEMU_CPU=${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512,zfh=true,zvfh=true}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 <binary-name-or-path> [args...]" >&2
    exit 1
fi

BIN=$1
shift
[ -f "$BIN" ] || BIN=$BIN_DIR/$BIN

MODEL=${MODEL:-$SCRIPT_DIR/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf}
case "$(basename "$BIN")" in
    llama-cli|llama-completion|llama-bench|llama-server|llama-perplexity)
        has_model=false
        for arg in "$@"; do
            [ "$arg" = "-m" ] && has_model=true
        done
        if ! $has_model; then
            set -- "$@" -m "$MODEL"
        fi
        ;;
esac

exec "$QEMU" \
    -L "$SYSROOT" \
    -E LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$BIN_DIR" \
    -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
    "$BIN" "$@"

content.content:
# Reproducing the Q1_0 RISC-V kernel optimizations

Four checks, cheapest first. Each one proves a different claim from the
summit abstract; run them in order and stop wherever you have enough
confidence.

| level | proves                                   | needs                | time     |
|-------|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------|----------|
| 1     | repack layout is numerically correct       | toolchain + qemu-user | ~1 min   |
| 2     | prefetch / `vd4dots` are actually emitted  | an existing build dir | ~1 min   |
| 3     | the shipped kernels reproduce upstream's text | andesim, fast mode  | ~8 min   |
| 4     | the cycle counts in the abstract           | andesim, hybrid + RTL | minutes/binary |

## Prerequisites

```bash
export LLAMA=~/work/llama.cpp
export ANDESIM=~/work/andesim
export TC=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d
cd "$LLAMA"

# confirm the pieces exist before running anything below
test -x "$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" && echo "toolchain: OK"
test -x "$ANDESIM/andesim"          && echo "andesim: OK"
test -f models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf  && echo "4B model: OK"
```

## Level 1 - repack layout correctness (qemu-user)

This checks the math, independent of the vendor instruction: pack random
weights, run the packed gemv/gemm, compare against a reference. Run it once
with the plain-RVV layout and once with the `vd4dots` layout - both must
pass, since they share the test and differ only in `D4`.

`o``bash
D4=0 bash build-d4-qemu.sh   # plain RVV layout (control)
D4=1 bash build-d4-qemu.sh   # vd4dots layout

QEMU_CPU=andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024,zfh=true,zvfh=true \
  BIN_DIR=build-d4-qemu/bin ./run-rv64-qemu.sh test-repack-q1_0
```

Expect `13/13 repack cases passed` both times. `D4=1`'s build directory is
overwritten by the second `build-d4-qemu.sh` call, so run the test between
the two builds if you want to see both pass lines separately.

These binaries are dynamic and built with a plain `-march` specifically so
qemu-user can run them directly. The `build.sh` binaries below (`bin-*`) are
static with the Zc compressed-instruction extensions, built for andesim -
qemu-user is not the right runner for those; use `run-rv64-qemu.sh` only on
`build-d4-qemu.sh` output.

## Level 2 - confirm the instructions are actually emitted

Correct output doesn't prove the fast path ran - a silently-generic fallback
gives the same numbers, just slower. These gates disassemble the built
object and count instructions.

```bash
bash build.sh prefetch d4     # needs the two builds these gates check

BUILD=b-prefetch ./check-prefetch.sh   # expects 2x prefetch.r per entry point
BUILD=b-d4        ./check-vd4dots.sh   # expects nds.vd4dots in gemv AND gemm,
                                        # no vtype churn, no strided broadcast
```

Both print `PASS: ...`. Either failing means the codegen regressed even
though Level 1's numbers still look right - that's the failure mode these
exist to catch.

## Level 3 - the shipped kernels reproduce upstream's output (andesim fast mode)

No RTL here. `--mode fast` is QEMU only - it stages the binary into a
`vlinux-run.elf`, boots `qemu-system-riscv64 -machine andes_ae350`, and
returns program output over semihosting. It runs the real model end to end
through `llama-completion` and compares the generated text of the two shipped
kernels against **upstream**:

| build      | flags                                       | role      |
|------------|---------------------------------------------|-----------|

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Codegen gate for the Q1_VD4DOT kernels (ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp).
3	#
4	# Two things this catches that no result test can:
5	#
6	#  1. A path silently falls back. Q1_VD4DOT changes the sign-plane order AND the
7	#     kernel; if gemv or gemm never got a vd4dots kernel it still returns
8	#     correct numbers through the generic C path, just ~3x slower. Counting
9	#     nds.vd4dots is the only way to see which one is really on the
10	#     instruction. (This was real: gemm ran generic for the whole F8 sweep.)
11	#
12	#  2. The F5 weight prefetch is dead-code eliminated. Same trap as
13	#     check-prefetch.sh guards, but that script counts per ENTRY point and the
14	#     d4 kernels stay out of line, so it reads 0 there and cannot be used on a
15	#     d4 build. Counted here instead, in the kernel body.
16	#
17	#  3. vtype churn (F9) creeps back. The kernels alternate between the byte
18	#     view (vlm, vmerge) and the 32-bit view (vmv.v.x, the dot), and every
19	#     alternation costs a vsetvli that does no arithmetic - 4 per dot in the
20	#     original gemv, 40% of its inner loop. The fix (batch by element width,
21	#     several dots per asm block) is invisible to every result test. Measured
22	#     as vsetvli between the FIRST and LAST dot, per dot gap, so the prologue
23	#     and the fp16-scale expansion do not pollute it. Budget: at most 1.
24	#
25	#  4. The activation broadcast collapses into vlse32.v vd,(rs1),zero. A
26	#     stride-0 strided load is element-serial on this core - 18x slower than
27	#     lw + vmv.v.x - and GCC contracts "load a word, splat it" into exactly
28	#     that whenever the value is not pinned in a GPR first (q1_bcast_act4).
29	#     Results are identical, so only the assembly shows it.
30	#
31	# The kernels are file-static, so each is checked in its own body; if the
32	# compiler inlined it away the entry point is checked instead. A kernel with
33	# no label and no inlined copy has been dead-code eliminated, which is exactly
34	# the "fell back to generic" failure.
35	#
36	# Reuses an existing CMake build's compile line for that one TU, so -march,
37	# -O level and includes are never duplicated here.
38	#
39	# Usage: ./check-vd4dots.sh [build-dir]      env: BUILD, OLEVELS
40	set -e
41	LLAMA=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
42	BUILD=${1:-${BUILD:-b-d4}}
43	OLEVELS=${OLEVELS:-"O2 O3 Os"}
44	SRC=$LLAMA/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp
45	# "<kernel static fn> <entry point it inlines into>"
46	KERNELS="q1_gemv_64_vd4dot_vl1024:ggml_gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0 q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024:ggml_gemm_q1_0_64x1_q8_0"
47	
48	CC_DB=$LLAMA/$BUILD/compile_commands.json
49	[ -f "$CC_DB" ] || { echo "no $CC_DB (build it with bash build.sh d4)"; exit 1; }
50	
51	ENTRY=$(python3 - "$CC_DB" <<'EOF'
52	import json, sys
53	for d in json.load(open(sys.argv[1])):
54	    if d['file'].endswith('arch/riscv/repack.cpp'):
55	        print(d['directory']); print(d['command']); break
56	else:
57	    sys.exit('arch/riscv/repack.cpp not in compile_commands.json')
58	EOF
59	)
60	CC_DIR=$(printf '%s' "$ENTRY" | head -1)
61	CC_CMD=$(printf '%s' "$ENTRY" | tail -1)
62	
63	case "$CC_CMD" in
64	    *xandesvdot*) ;;
65	    *) echo "$BUILD is not an XAndesVDot build (-march has no xandesvdot)"; exit 1 ;;
66	esac
67	case "$CC_CMD" in
68	    *-DQ1_VD4DOT=1*) ;;
69	    *) echo "$BUILD is not a Q1_VD4DOT build"; exit 1 ;;
70	esac
71	# a deliberate DIST=0 build (b-d4-nopf) has no prefetch to find
72	WANT_PF=1
73	case "$CC_CMD" in *-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0*) WANT_PF=0 ;; esac
74	
75	OUT=$LLAMA/$BUILD/vd4dots-check
76	mkdir -p "$OUT"
77	echo "build $BUILD, source $SRC"
78	
79	rc=0
80	
81	# label of function $1 in $2: the plain name, or its C++ static mangling
82	label_of() {
83	    awk -v N="$1" '/^[A-Za-z_].*:$/ {
84	        s = substr($0, 1, length($0)-1)
85	        if (s == N || (s ~ /^_ZL[0-9]+/ && index(s, N) > 0)) { print s; exit }
86	    }' "$2"
87	}
88	
89	# count instructions matching $2 inside the body of label $1 in file $3
90	count_in() {
91	    awk -v F="$1:" -v P="$2" 'BEGIN{c=0} $0==F{i=1;next} i&&$0~P{c++} i&&/[.]size/{i=0} END{print c}' "$3"
92	}
93	
94	# "<vsetvli between first and last dot> <dot gaps>" for label $1 in file $2
95	vset_span() {
96	    awk -v F="$1:" 'BEGIN{d=0;v=0;last=0}
97	        $0==F{i=1;next} i&&/[.]size/{i=0}
98	        i&&/nds[.]vd4dots/{d++; if(d==1)on=1; last=v}
99	        i&&on&&/vset[a-z]*vli/{v++}
100	        END{print last, (d>1?d-1:0)}' "$2"
101	}
102	
103	# $1 = label, $2 = -O level to force ("" = keep the build's own)
104	check_variant() {
105	    asm=$OUT/repack-$1.s
106	    cmd=$CC_CMD
107	    [ -n "$2" ] && cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -E "s/ -O[0-9sgz]+ / -$2 /")
108	    cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -E "s#-o [^ ]+[.]o #-S -o $asm #")
109	    ( cd "$CC_DIR" && eval "$cmd" )
110	
111	    line="  $1:"
112	    for ke in $KERNELS; do
113	        kern=${ke%%:*}
114	        sym=$(label_of "$kern" "$asm")
115	        [ -n "$sym" ] || sym=${ke##*:}          # inlined into the entry point
116	        dot=$(count_in "$sym" 'nds[.]vd4dots' "$asm")
117	        lse=$(count_in "$sym" 'vlse[0-9]+[.]v' "$asm")
118	        pf=$(count_in  "$sym" 'prefetch[.]'   "$asm")
119	        set -- $(vset_span "$sym" "$asm")
120	        vs=$1; gaps=$2
121	        line="$line  $kern=dot$dot/pf$pf/lse$lse/vset$vs:$gaps"
122	        [ "$gaps" -gt 0 ] && [ "$vs" -gt "$gaps" ] && { line="$line(VTYPE-CHURN)"; rc=1; }
123	        [ "$dot" -eq 0 ] && { line="$line(NO-DOT)"; rc=1; }
124	        [ "$pf"  -eq 0 ] && [ "$WANT_PF" = 1 ] && { line="$line(NO-PREFETCH)"; rc=1; }
125	        [ "$lse" -gt 0 ] && { line="$line(STRIDED)"; rc=1; }
126	    done
127	    echo "$line"
128	}
129	
130	check_variant "as-built" ""
131	for o in $OLEVELS; do check_variant "-$o" "$o"; done
132	
133	if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
134	    echo "FAIL: NO-DOT       = that kernel is not on nds.vd4dots (generic C fallback)."
135	    echo "      NO-PREFETCH  = ipa-pure-const + DCE ate q1_prefetch_block;"
136	    echo "                     check always_inline on it and zicbop in -march."
137	    echo "      VTYPE-CHURN  = more than one vsetvli per dot in the steady state"
138	    echo "                     (F9). Batch the e8 work and the e32 work, and put"
139	    echo "                     several dots in one asm block."
140	    echo "      STRIDED      = the activation broadcast became vlse32.v ...,zero;"
141	    echo "                     check the asm(\"\" : \"+r\"(w)) barrier in q1_bcast_act4."
142	    exit 1
143	fi
144	echo "PASS: gemv and gemm both use nds.vd4dots, prefetch, no strided load, at ($OLEVELS)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Codegen gate for the Q1_VD4DOT kernels (ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp).
#
# Two things this catches that no result test can:
#
#  1. A path silently falls back. Q1_VD4DOT changes the sign-plane order AND the
#     kernel; if gemv or gemm never got a vd4dots kernel it still returns
#     correct numbers through the generic C path, just ~3x slower. Counting
#     nds.vd4dots is the only way to see which one is really on the
#     instruction. (This was real: gemm ran generic for the whole F8 sweep.)
#
#  2. The F5 weight prefetch is dead-code eliminated. Same trap as
#     check-prefetch.sh guards, but that script counts per ENTRY point and the
#     d4 kernels stay out of line, so it reads 0 there and cannot be used on a
#     d4 build. Counted here instead, in the kernel body.
#
#  3. vtype churn (F9) creeps back. The kernels alternate between the byte
#     view (vlm, vmerge) and the 32-bit view (vmv.v.x, the dot), and every
#     alternation costs a vsetvli that does no arithmetic - 4 per dot in the
#     original gemv, 40% of its inner loop. The fix (batch by element width,
#     several dots per asm block) is invisible to every result test. Measured
#     as vsetvli between the FIRST and LAST dot, per dot gap, so the prologue
#     and the fp16-scale expansion do not pollute it. Budget: at most 1.
#
#  4. The activation broadcast collapses into vlse32.v vd,(rs1),zero. A
#     stride-0 strided load is element-serial on this core - 18x slower than
#     lw + vmv.v.x - and GCC contracts "load a word, splat it" into exactly
#     that whenever the value is not pinned in a GPR first (q1_bcast_act4).
#     Results are identical, so only the assembly shows it.
#
# The kernels are file-static, so each is checked in its own body; if the
# compiler inlined it away the entry point is checked instead. A kernel with
# no label and no inlined copy has been dead-code eliminated, which is exactly
# the "fell back to generic" failure.
#
# Reuses an existing CMake build's compile line for that one TU, so -march,
# -O level and includes are never duplicated here.
#
# Usage: ./check-vd4dots.sh [build-dir]      env: BUILD, OLEVELS
set -e
LLAMA=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
BUILD=${1:-${BUILD:-b-d4}}
OLEVELS=${OLEVELS:-"O2 O3 Os"}
SRC=$LLAMA/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp
# "<kernel static fn> <entry point it inlines into>"
KERNELS="q1_gemv_64_vd4dot_vl1024:ggml_gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0 q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024:ggml_gemm_q1_0_64x1_q8_0"

CC_DB=$LLAMA/$BUILD/compile_commands.json
[ -f "$CC_DB" ] || { echo "no $CC_DB (build it with bash build.sh d4)"; exit 1; }

ENTRY=$(python3 - "$CC_DB" <<'EOF'
import json, sys
for d in json.load(open(sys.argv[1])):
    if d['file'].endswith('arch/riscv/repack.cpp'):
        print(d['directory']); print(d['command']); break
else:
    sys.exit('arch/riscv/repack.cpp not in compile_commands.json')
EOF
)
CC_DIR=$(printf '%s' "$ENTRY" | head -1)
CC_CMD=$(printf '%s' "$ENTRY" | tail -1)

case "$CC_CMD" in
    *xandesvdot*) ;;
    *) echo "$BUILD is not an XAndesVDot build (-march has no xandesvdot)"; exit 1 ;;
esac
case "$CC_CMD" in
    *-DQ1_VD4DOT=1*) ;;
    *) echo "$BUILD is not a Q1_VD4DOT build"; exit 1 ;;
esac
# a deliberate DIST=0 build (b-d4-nopf) has no prefetch to find
WANT_PF=1
case "$CC_CMD" in *-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0*) WANT_PF=0 ;; esac

OUT=$LLAMA/$BUILD/vd4dots-check
mkdir -p "$OUT"
echo "build $BUILD, source $SRC"

rc=0

# label of function $1 in $2: the plain name, or its C++ static mangling
label_of() {
    awk -v N="$1" '/^[A-Za-z_].*:$/ {
        s = substr($0, 1, length($0)-1)
        if (s == N || (s ~ /^_ZL[0-9]+/ && index(s, N) > 0)) { print s; exit }
    }' "$2"
}

# count instructions matching $2 inside the body of label $1 in file $3
count_in() {
    awk -v F="$1:" -v P="$2" 'BEGIN{c=0} $0==F{i=1;next} i&&$0~P{c++} i&&/[.]size/{i=0} END{print c}' "$3"
}

# "<vsetvli between first and last dot> <dot gaps>" for label $1 in file $2
vset_span() {
    awk -v F="$1:" 'BEGIN{d=0;v=0;last=0}
        $0==F{i=1;next} i&&/[.]size/{i=0}
        i&&/nds[.]vd4dots/{d++; if(d==1)on=1; last=v}
        i&&on&&/vset[a-z]*vli/{v++}
        END{print last, (d>1?d-1:0)}' "$2"
}

# $1 = label, $2 = -O level to force ("" = keep the build's own)
check_variant() {
    asm=$OUT/repack-$1.s
    cmd=$CC_CMD
    [ -n "$2" ] && cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -E "s/ -O[0-9sgz]+ / -$2 /")
    cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | sed -E "s#-o [^ ]+[.]o #-S -o $asm #")
    ( cd "$CC_DIR" && eval "$cmd" )

    line="  $1:"
    for ke in $KERNELS; do
        kern=${ke%%:*}
        sym=$(label_of "$kern" "$asm")
        [ -n "$sym" ] || sym=${ke##*:}          # inlined into the entry point
        dot=$(count_in "$sym" 'nds[.]vd4dots' "$asm")
        lse=$(count_in "$sym" 'vlse[0-9]+[.]v' "$asm")
        pf=$(count_in  "$sym" 'prefetch[.]'   "$asm")
        set -- $(vset_span "$sym" "$asm")
        vs=$1; gaps=$2
        line="$line  $kern=dot$dot/pf$pf/lse$lse/vset$vs:$gaps"
        [ "$gaps" -gt 0 ] && [ "$vs" -gt "$gaps" ] && { line="$line(VTYPE-CHURN)"; rc=1; }
        [ "$dot" -eq 0 ] && { line="$line(NO-DOT)"; rc=1; }
        [ "$pf"  -eq 0 ] && [ "$WANT_PF" = 1 ] && { line="$line(NO-PREFETCH)"; rc=1; }
        [ "$lse" -gt 0 ] && { line="$line(STRIDED)"; rc=1; }
    done
    echo "$line"
}

check_variant "as-built" ""
for o in $OLEVELS; do check_variant "-$o" "$o"; done

if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL: NO-DOT       = that kernel is not on nds.vd4dots (generic C fallback)."
    echo "      NO-PREFETCH  = ipa-pure-const + DCE ate q1_prefetch_block;"
    echo "                     check always_inline on it and zicbop in -march."
    echo "      VTYPE-CHURN  = more than one vsetvli per dot in the steady state"
    echo "                     (F9). Batch the e8 work and the e32 work, and put"
    echo "                     several dots in one asm block."
    echo "      STRIDED      = the activation broadcast became vlse32.v ...,zero;"
    echo "                     check the asm(\"\" : \"+r\"(w)) barrier in q1_bcast_act4."
    exit 1
fi
echo "PASS: gemv and gemm both use nds.vd4dots, prefetch, no strided load, at ($OLEVELS)"

[ -f "$GGUF" ] || { echo "no such model: $GGUF" >&2; exit 1; }

gen() {  # $1 = binary -> the line holding the prompt and its continuation
  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size "$MEM" \
      --engine "$ENGINE" "$1" -- -m "$GGUF" $MMAP -no-cnv \
      --prompt "$PROMPT" -n "$NGEN" -c 512 -t 1 --temp 0 ) 2>&1 \
    | grep "$PROMPT" | head -1
}

# llama-completion echoes the prompt before it generates (display_prompt
# defaults true), so two runs that both produced ZERO tokens would compare
# equal and non-empty. Require the line to be longer than the prompt it echoed.
run() {  # $1 = build name -> its line, or exit 1
  local bin="$LLAMA/bin-$1" line
  [ -x "$bin" ] || { echo "missing build: $bin (run: bash build.sh $1)" >&2; exit 1; }
  line=$(gen "$bin")
  [ ${#line} -gt ${#PROMPT} ] || { echo "FAIL: $1 generated no tokens" >&2; exit 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$line"
}

label() { printf '%-9s %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'):" "$2"; }

echo "model: $GGUF   ref: $REF   engine: $ENGINE"
R=$(run "$REF")
label "$REF" "$R"

rc=0
for t in ${*:-prefetch d4}; do
  O=$(run "$t")
  label "$t" "$O"
  if [ "$O" = "$R" ]; then
    echo "PASS: $t output is identical to $REF"
  else
    echo "FAIL: $t output differs from $REF"
    rc=1
  fi
done
exit $rc

#       repack layout or the prefetch helper's address math is wrong.
#
#   d4 vs pristine  Not guaranteed bit-for-bit. The gemv keeps the nesting
#       above, so decode is exact, but the vd4dot GEMM folds dx*ad[m] into each q8
#       group and accumulates into sumf 4x per block (q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024)
#       where the others build facc first and accumulate once per block. That
#       is a different rounding order, so PREFILL floats differ at the ULP
#       level by construction. Equal greedy text is the acceptance bar; if it
#       ever fails, compare tensors with a tolerance, do not hunt a logic bug.
#
# Minutes per binary. Override via env LLAMA / ANDESIM / MODEL / REF / PROMPT / NGEN.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
# --engine is NOT cosmetic in fast mode: it picks QEMU's -cpu and VLEN.
# vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 -> andes-ax46mpv,vlen=1024; omitting it falls back to

**Verification** - this was a pure rename (REFACTOR), so both gates ran before and after:

| gate | before | after |
|---|---|---|

The codegen gate is the strong one: it found both kernels by their *new* names and still counted `nds.vd4dots` + prefetch + no strided load, so the rename is consistent from CMake through the source to the emitted assembly.

**Two things I deliberately left alone:**

1. **Build target and directory names** (`build.sh d4`, `b-d4`, `bin-d4`, and verify.sh's `D4:` output label, which is just the uppercased target name). Renaming these would invalidate 14 existing build trees and break the references in `profiling_data.md` / `q1_0_8b_hybrid.md` / `opt_roadmap.md` that point at already-recorded measurements. Say the word if you want them renamed too.
2. **`nds.vd4dots` vs `vd4dot`** - the real mnemonic has a trailing `s` (signed variant). I used `VD4DOT` as you wrote it, which also matches the existing `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT` CMake flag.

One side effect: I reconfigured `b-d4` so its `compile_commands.json` carries `-DQ1_VD4DOT=1`. The other `b-d4-k*` dirs still have the old macro cached and will need a reconfigure before `check-vd4dots.sh` accepts them.

content.text:
4 dots = 4 column quads = **16 columns** of the same 64 rows, all accumulated into one `acc`.

## What the block covers

```
nds.vd4dots.vv acc, w0, s0   <- columns c+0..c+3    each dot: 64 rows x 4 cols
nds.vd4dots.vv acc, w1, s1   <- columns c+4..c+7
nds.vd4dots.vv acc, w2, s0   <- columns c+8..c+11
nds.vd4dots.vv acc, w3, s1   <- columns c+12..c+15
```

One Q8_0 group is 32 columns = 8 quads, so the loop at `repack.cpp:1887` runs **2 blocks per group**: `for (q = 0; q < QK8_0/4; q += 4)`.

## Why 4 and not 1

`vsetvli` amortization (the F9 fix). GCC cannot see inside an `asm` block, so it assumes vtype is unknown afterwards and re-issues its own `vsetvli` before the next intrinsic. The kernel alternates two element widths - e8 for the mask load + sign expand, e32 for the broadcast + dot - so one dot per block cost 4 `vsetvli` per dot, about 40% of the inner loop and none of it arithmetic.

Putting all the e32 work (the `vmv.v.x` broadcasts too) inside one block leaves GCC only e8 work to schedule. The emitted O2 loop confirms it - 2 `vsetvli` per 4 dots:

```
171:  vsetvli zero,a5,e8,m2,ta,ma      <- GCC, for the 4 vlm + vmerge
176:  vsetvli t0, zero, e32, m2,ta,ma  <- ours, inside the asm
177:  vmv.v.x v22, s10
178:  vmv.v.x v24, s11
179:  nds.vd4dots.vv v2, v6,  v22
180:  nds.vd4dots.vv v2, v8,  v24
181:  vmv.v.x v22, t4
182:  vmv.v.x v24, s9
183:  nds.vd4dots.vv v2, v10, v22
184:  nds.vd4dots.vv v2, v12, v24
187:  vsetvli zero,a5,e8,m2,ta,ma      <- next block
```

0.5 `vsetvli` per dot, down from 4.

## Why 4 and not 8

Register budget at LMUL=2. Four weight vectors cost 8 registers, plus 2 scratch (4 registers) and the accumulator (2) = 14. Eight weights would be 22 before counting anything else - and the gemm twin `q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2` (`repack.cpp:1831`) needs 4 accumulators on top. That is also why there are only **two** scratch vectors `s0`/`s1` reloaded mid-block rather than four: enough for the dots to still overlap, cheap enough to leave the gemm room.

`check-vd4dots.sh` guards this - it counts `vsetvli` between the first and last dot and fails on more than one per dot gap.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fast-mode whole-model check for q1_0_reproduce.md Level 3.
#
# Runs the three configurations that actually ship, under andesim --mode fast
# (QEMU only - functional, no cycle leg), greedy, same prompt, and compares
# each optimized build's generated text against upstream's:
#
#   pristine  GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF                      <- the reference
#   prefetch  repack + weight-stream prefetch (DIST=1)
#   d4        repack + prefetch + nds.vd4dots.vv
#
#   bash verify.sh                  # 4b model, prefetch and d4 vs pristine
#   MODEL=8b bash verify.sh         # same, on Bonsai-8B
#   MODEL=27b bash verify.sh
#   MODEL=/path/to/x.gguf bash verify.sh
#   REF=baseline bash verify.sh prefetch    # isolate the prefetch hint alone
#
# Why equality is the right bar, per comparison:
#
#   prefetch vs pristine  Expected to match exactly. Upstream's VLEN>=256 path
#       (ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0_vl256) reduces as `acc += d1*sumi` per q8 group
#       then `sumf += d0*acc` per block, and the repack gemv uses that same
#       nesting (facc per group, sumf per block). prefetch.r on top is an
#       architectural hint and cannot change a result, so a mismatch means the
#       repack layout or the prefetch helper's address math is wrong.
#
#   d4 vs pristine  Not guaranteed bit-for-bit. The gemv keeps the nesting
#       above, so decode is exact, but the vd4dot GEMM folds dx*ad[m] into
#       each q8 group and accumulates into sumf 4x per block
#       (q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024)
#       where the others build facc first and accumulate once per block. That
#       is a different rounding order, so PREFILL floats differ at the ULP
#       level by construction. Equal greedy text is the acceptance bar; if it
#       ever fails, compare tensors with a tolerance, do not hunt a logic bug.
#
# Minutes per binary. Override via env LLAMA / ANDESIM / MODEL / REF / PROMPT / NGEN.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
# --engine is NOT cosmetic in fast mode: it picks QEMU's -cpu and VLEN.
# vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 -> andes-ax46mpv,vlen=1024; omitting it falls back to
# andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, where q1_gemv_64_vd4dot_vl1024 does not apply and the
# d4 build silently drops to the generic kernel - the comparison would still PASS
# while testing nothing. Keep this at a VLEN>=1024 engine.
ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
REF=${REF:-pristine}
PROMPT=${PROMPT:-The capital of France is}
NGEN=${NGEN:-16}

# Model selection. The bigger models need more guest RAM than the 4B, and need
# --no-mmap because the mapped file does not fit the guest window. These are
# FAST-mode sizes: unlike hybrid, fast mode has no 2G cap (it is just QEMU's
# -m), but QEMU takes whole MiB - the hybrid runbook's 2097148K is rejected here.
case "${MODEL:-4b}" in
  4b)  GGUF="$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf";  MEM=${MEM:-2000M}; MMAP="" ;;
  8b)  GGUF="$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf";  MEM=${MEM:-4G};    MMAP="--no-mmap" ;;
  27b) GGUF="$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf"; MEM=${MEM:-8G};    MMAP="--no-mmap" ;;
  *)   GGUF="$MODEL";                             MEM=${MEM:-8G};    MMAP="--no-mmap" ;;
esac
[ -f "$GGUF" ] || { echo "no such model: $GGUF" >&2; exit 1; }

gen() {  # $1 = binary -> the line holding the prompt and its continuation
  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size "$MEM" \
      --engine "$ENGINE" "$1" -- -m "$GGUF" $MMAP -no-cnv \
      --prompt "$PROMPT" -n "$NGEN" -c 512 -t 1 --temp 0 ) 2>&1 \
    | grep "$PROMPT" | head -1
}

# llama-completion echoes the prompt before it generates (display_prompt
# defaults true), so two runs that both produced ZERO tokens would compare
# equal and non-empty. Require the line to be longer than the prompt it echoed.
run() {  # $1 = build name -> its line, or exit 1
  local bin="$LLAMA/bin-$1" line
  [ -x "$bin" ] || { echo "missing build: $bin (run: bash build.sh $1)" >&2; exit 1; }
  line=$(gen "$bin")
  [ ${#line} -gt ${#PROMPT} ] || { echo "FAIL: $1 generated no tokens" >&2; exit 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$line"
}

label() { printf '%-9s %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'):" "$2"; }

echo "model: $GGUF   ref: $REF   engine: $ENGINE"
R=$(run "$REF")
label "$REF" "$R"

rc=0
for t in ${*:-prefetch d4}; do
  O=$(run "$t")
  label "$t" "$O"
  if [ "$O" = "$R" ]; then
    echo "PASS: $t output is identical to $REF"
  else
    echo "FAIL: $t output differs from $REF"
    rc=1
  fi
done
exit $rc

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Correctness build for the Q1_0 nds.vd4dots (Q1_VD4DOT) kernel: rv64 + RVV,
# runs under Andes user-mode QEMU. Pair with:
#   QEMU_CPU=andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024,zfh=true,zvfh=true \
#   BIN_DIR=build-vd4dot-qemu/bin ./run-rv64-qemu.sh test-repack-q1_0
#
#   bash build-vd4dot-qemu.sh          # vd4dot layout + nds.vd4dots kernel
#   VD4DOT=0 bash build-vd4dot-qemu.sh # same tree, stock layout (control)
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}
VD4DOT=${VD4DOT:-1}
DIR=${DIR:-$LLAMA/build-vd4dot-qemu}

FL="-march=rv64gcv -mext-zvlsseg -DQ1_VD4DOT=$VD4DOT"
cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$DIR" \
  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \
  -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON \
  -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
cmake --build "$DIR" --target test-repack-q1_0 -j"$(nproc)"
echo "built: $DIR/bin/test-repack-q1_0 (Q1_VD4DOT=$VD4DOT)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hybrid K=51 ROI cycle measurement for the prefetch reproduce runbook
# (q1_0_hvm_reproduce.md). Prints, per binary, the [roi] self-check line
# (now including nrows) and the [andesim] <N> cycles figure for the K=51 node.
#
#   bash measure.sh                     # pristine baseline prefetch (gemv/decode node)
#   bash measure.sh baseline prefetch   # just the prefetch A/B
#   PROMPT="The capital of France" WARMUP=--no-warmup bash measure.sh baseline prefetch
#                                       # pure-gemm node (nrows=4): measures the gemm path
#
# GEMV (decode) node = the warmup forward pass, nrows=2. Expected K=51 cycles:
#   pristine 4,476,168 -> baseline 2,144,213 -> prefetch 1,391,650
#   (prefetch = 1.54x vs baseline, 3.22x vs pristine)
# GEMM (prefill) node = --no-warmup + a 4-token prompt, nrows=4 (pure gemm):
#   baseline 1,696,704 -> prefetch 1,649,275 (only 1.03x - gemm reuses each
#   weight block across the M-tile of 4, so it is ~compute-bound, little to hide)
#   pristine 8,875,248 -> prefetch 1,651,949 -> d4 931,754 -> d4+F9 818,314
#   (10.85x over pristine). K=56 ffn_down: prefetch 13,474,132 -> d4 6,636,852
#   -> d4+F9 5,683,029. d4 beats prefetch by more on ffn_down (2.03x vs 1.77x)
#   because 3.5 MB does not fit the 2 MB L3, so weight reuse still buys memory
#   traffic there.
#   Decode for comparison: pristine 4,476,673 -> prefetch 1,389,236 ->
#   d4 457,092 -> d4+F9 362,799 (12.34x over pristine).
#
#
# Other shapes: the measured node is compile-time (see build.sh ROI_K), so a
# shape sweep passes the suffixed binaries, e.g.
#   bash measure.sh pristine-k54 baseline-k54 prefetch-k54   # blk.7.ffn_gate
# Bonsai-4B has 6 distinct Q1_0 shapes; layer 7 covers all of them at
# ROI_K = 50 attn_q / 51 attn_v / 52 attn_k / 53 attn_output / 54 ffn_gate /
# 55 ffn_up / 56 ffn_down. Cost scales with rows*K, so ffn_* is ~9.5x the
# attn_v node -> raise TIMEOUT for those.
#
# Slow: the RTL leg runs at a few kHz -> minutes per binary. Override via env
# LLAMA / ANDESIM / MODEL / ENGINE / PROMPT / WARMUP / TIMEOUT.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
MODEL=${MODEL:-$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}
ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
PROMPT=${PROMPT:-The capital of France is}
WARMUP=${WARMUP:-}
TIMEOUT=${TIMEOUT:-14400000}   # hybrid per-leg spawn timeout, ms (4h)

for b in ${*:-pristine baseline prefetch}; do
  echo "=== $b ==="
  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
      --mem-size 2000M --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms "$TIMEOUT" \
      "$LLAMA/bin-$b" -- -m "$MODEL" -no-cnv $WARMUP --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 ) 2>&1 | grep -E '\[roi\]|\[andesim\] .*cycles'
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the RISC-V llama-completion binaries for the Q1_0 kernel A/Bs:
#   pristine = upstream kernel, no repack
#   baseline = repack row-parallel kernel, prefetch OFF (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0)
#   prefetch = repack + weight-stream prefetch, the shipped kernel (DIST=1)
#   d4       = repack + prefetch + nds.vd4dots.vv kernels (XAndesVDot)
#   d4-nopf  = d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF
#
#   bash build.sh                    # pristine baseline prefetch
#   bash build.sh d4                 # the vd4dots kernel
#   bash build.sh baseline prefetch  # the prefetch A/B pair
#
# Override paths via env: LLAMA, ANDESIM, TC.
set -e
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}   # /tmp inodes are exhausted -> ENOSPC without this
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
TC=${TC:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d}

# Which MUL_MAT node the ROI brackets. Compile-time because andesim's linux
# runtime hands the guest an EMPTY envp (runtime/linux/stack.h), so the
# GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K env override never reaches the guest -- one binary per
# measured node. Bonsai-4B layer 7 shape table:
#   50 attn_q  51 attn_v  52 attn_k  53 attn_output  54 ffn_gate  55 ffn_up
#   56 ffn_down                                       253 result_output
# K=51 keeps the original unsuffixed artifact names; anything else appends -k<K>.
ROI_K=${ROI_K:-51}
SUF=""; [ "$ROI_K" = 51 ] || SUF="-k$ROI_K"

# The settings that MUST be right (else the guest crashes / baseline is wrong):
#   -static                  : vlinux proxy kernel has no dynamic loader
#   -DGGML_CPU_REPACK        : a CMake option(), passed as a top-level -D (NOT in *_FLAGS)
#   -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON      : lets __builtin_prefetch emit prefetch.r for the Q1_0
#                              gemv weight-stream prefetch (Q1_PREFETCH_DIST, 1.54x on K=51)
#   -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON  : single switch for the vd4dot kernels - appends _xandesvdot
#                              to -march AND defines Q1_VD4DOT (kernels + sign-plane order)
#   -DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=N     : prefetch lookahead in blocks; 0 = off (baseline), 1 = shipped
cfg() {  # $1 build dir   $2 repack/vdot toggles   $3 extra defines (DIST etc., or "")
  local FL="$3 -mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM/build/runtime/include"
  cmake -S "$LLAMA" -B "$1" \
    -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Linux -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=riscv64 \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$TC/bin/riscv64-linux-g++" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF \
    -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
    -DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON \
    -DGGML_CCACHE=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-static \
    $2 -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FL" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FL"
  cmake --build "$1" --target llama-completion -j"$(nproc)"
}

build_one() {  # $1 = pristine | baseline | prefetch | d4 | d4-nopf | *-nodpref
  case "$1" in
    pristine) cfg "$LLAMA/b-pristine$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF" "" ;;
    baseline) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    prefetch) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON"  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 = the shipped kernel with the K-reduction handed to nds.vd4dots.vv.
    # GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT is the whole switch: -march plus the Q1_VD4DOT source gate
    # (kernels and sign-plane repack order), so no extra define is needed.
    d4)       cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1" ;;
    # d4 with the weight-stream prefetch OFF. Answers "is the vd4dot kernel still
    # memory-bound?" - if this lands near d4, the weight stream is fully hidden
    # and there is nothing left for a bigger/faster memory to recover.
    d4-nopf)  cfg "$LLAMA/b-d4-nopf$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON -DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON" \
                  "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0" ;;
    # A/B pair for "does prefetch.r depend on the D$ prefetch unit": same
    # kernels, but the ROI runs with mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN cleared.
    prefetch-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-prefetch-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=1 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    baseline-nodpref) cfg "$LLAMA/b-baseline-nodpref$SUF" "-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=ON" "-DQ1_PREFETCH_DIST=0 -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF" ;;
    *) echo "unknown target '$1' (want pristine|baseline|prefetch|d4|d4-nopf|*-nodpref)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  cp "$LLAMA/b-$1$SUF/bin/llama-completion" "$LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF"
  echo "built: $LLAMA/bin-$1$SUF (ROI MUL_MAT #$ROI_K)"
}

for t in ${*:-pristine baseline prefetch}; do build_one "$t"; done

## Attention layer (`blk.7`) -- 16 of 64 layers

The five nodes with all four stages measured.

| step | geo mean | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream to standard RVV -- portable, any RVV core | **3.57x** | 3.33x | 4.11x |
| standard RVV to vd4dots -- Andes V5 XAndesVDot | **3.54x** | 3.47x | 3.59x |
| **total** | **12.64x** | | |

## Notes

- `ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` get **no speedup at all** (1.00x). They have 48 rows and
  the repack gate requires `ne[1] %% 64 == 0`, so both builds run the stock kernel.
  They are the only two gate failures in the model: 0.09%% of the weights but 1.7%% of
  the optimized cycles. Padding them to 64 rows would recover about 1%% of a token.
- Identical shapes give identical cycles **once optimized**. `ssm_out` and
  `attn_output` are both 6144 x 5120: 0.037%% apart at vd4dots, **2.63%% apart at
  upstream**. The stock kernel is sensitive to where in the graph a node sits; the

  column carries roughly 2.6%% uncertainty while their vd4dots column does not.

  which is the run-to-run noise floor here.
- Optimization compresses the spread. Upstream costs 1.75-2.14 cycles per weight
  across these shapes (22%% spread); vd4dots costs 0.144-0.158 (9%% spread).

9	  compute buffers (27B needs ~4.5 GB - blocked until andesim grows >2 GiB

18	- vsim:ax45mpv_premium - VLEN=512, DLEN=512, ELEN=32, no zfh/zvfh.
19	- vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 - VLEN=1024, ELEN=64, first engine with real L3.

22	- QEMU proxy (insn-count, -t 8, build-rv64-noomp, 2026-07-15):
23	  4B ~19-21 s/token. QEMU time tracks instruction count, not latency.

26	  - ax45mpv_premium: 6528953 cycles (2026-07-16, stable across runs)
27	  - ax46mpv_fpga_l3: 4476168 cycles (2026-07-16, pristine upstream ggml)

29	  real pipeline + memory system.
30	
31	Rules for every feature below:
32	- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
33	  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
34	  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.

50	## F1. Q1_0 multi-row vec_dot (nrows = 2)
51	
52	- Status: TODO

55	  output elements: load + negate activations once, per row only do mask

70	  repack) solves the actual problem and makes this path dead weight.

72	  makes scalar ops ~free, so this kind of stall-removal restructure READS
73	  AS A REGRESSION under QEMU (n=8192: vl256 57.5us vs vl512 75.5us) -
74	  never judge restructures by QEMU; only vsim/FPGA cycles count.

79	  contiguous (34-byte block stride), filling a 512-bit register costs slide
80	  instructions that cancel the saved vlm/vneg/vmerge. Wider vl alone cannot
81	  win for the vec_dot shape; width pays off only via repack (F4, contiguous
82	  interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1). Not a standalone feature.
83	
84	## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)
85	
86	- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-22) - F4a DONE, F4b lab-verified pending
87	  cycle gate; largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
88	- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
89	  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
90	  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
91	  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
92	    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
93	    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
94	    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
95	    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
96	  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
97	    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
98	    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
99	    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
100	    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
101	    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
102	- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
103	  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
104	  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
105	    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
106	  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
107	- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
108	  ```
109	  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
110	  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
111	      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
112	      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
113	      for c in 0..31:
114	          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
115	          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
116	          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes
117	          sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask, sumi, 2*y)          // +2y where bit set => +-y
118	      facc_block = vfmacc_vf(facc_block, dy, vfcvt(sumi))   // scalar dy
119	  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
120	  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs

563	     the only thing that shows it; prefetch.r > 0 - the F5 DCE trap; vlse* == 0
564	     - trap 1 below.
565	  3. End to end: andesim --mode fast, greedy, Bonsai-4B - d4 and the shipped
566	     prefetch binary generate byte-identical text. Re-run for the gemm with a
567	     20-token prompt (5 gemm row tiles through all 36 layers, and ffn_down's
568	     39 KB activation staging buffer): "The capital of France is Paris and the
569	     capital of Japan is Tokyo and the capital of Italy is Rome. The capital
570	     of the United States is Washington, D.C. and the".
571	- Key files:
572	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.h: `q1_0x64_sign_bit` (the one layout authority)
573	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp: repack writer + both generic readers use it
574	  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp: `q1_vd4dots_m2`,
575	    `q1_bcast_act4`, `q1_gemv_64_vd4dot_vl1024`, `q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024`
576	  - ggml/CMakeLists.txt + ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt: GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT
577	  - build.sh `d4` target; build-vd4dot-qemu.sh for the QEMU correctness build
578	  - check-vd4dots.sh: the codegen gate (dot / prefetch / no-strided-load)
579	- Next levers, in order of expected value:
580	  1. F9, vtype churn - DONE 2026-08-01, see below. Was: measured from the O3
581	     assembly, per nds.vd4dots issued:
582	       gemv  80 instrs / 8 dots = 10.0, of which 4.0 are vsetvli (40%)
583	       gemm  36 instrs / 4 dots =  9.0, of which 2.5 are vsetvli (28%)
584	     CAUSE, and it is NOT mainly the inline asm - it is e8/e32 ping-pong. One
585	     real gemv column at O3:
586	       vlm.v v0,0(t0)            # mask                          e8
587	       lw t0,4(t5)
588	       vsetvli zero,a4,e32,m2                                #  -> e32
589	       vmv.v.x v16,t0            # broadcast 4 activations
590	       vsetvli zero,a5,e8,m2                                 #  -> e8
591	       vmerge.vim v10,v4,1,v0    # mask -> +-1 bytes
592	       vsetvli t0,zero,e32,m2    # (inside the asm)          #  -> e32
593	       nds.vd4dots.vv v2,v10,v16 # the only real work
594	       addi t0,a6,64
595	       vsetvli zero,a5,e8,m2                                 #  -> e8, next vlm
596	     Ten instructions, one of which multiplies. The work genuinely alternates
597	     between the byte view (mask, merge) and the 32-bit view (broadcast, dot),
598	     and each alternation costs one vsetvli; GCC re-emitting after the asm
599	     (because it cannot see the asm left vtype at e32/m2) is only ONE of the
600	     four. So widening the asm block alone recovers 1 of 4, not 4 of 4.
601	     FIX: batch by element width, not by column - do 4 columns of e8 work
602	     under one vsetvli, then 4 columns of e32 work under one more, with the 4
603	     dots in a single asm block. 4 dots go from 40 instrs / 16 vsetvli to ~26
604	     / 2, about 1.5x on the gemv. Register cost there is mild (4 live weight
605	     vectors = 8 of 32, and the gemv tracks one output row), so it fits; the
606	     gemm is tighter (4 sumf + 4 acc = 16 already) and may only batch 2.
607	     CAVEAT: this is an instruction count, not cycles. vsetvli is cheap, so
608	     expect less than the ratio suggests. Nothing built or measured yet.
609	  2. VLEN=512 (premium) shape: e32/m4. Blocked on the ax45 hybrid halt bug.
610	  3. The other unexplored vendor ops in fpga_l3's ISA string: nds.vqmacc.*,
611	     nds.vln8.v / nds.vle4.v sub-int loads, nds.vfpmadb/t.vf, nds.vfwcvt.f.b.v.
612	  4. Prefill shape sweep: only attn_v and ffn_down were measured with nrows=4.
613	     The other 5 layer-7 nodes are unmeasured for prefill, and unlike the gemv
614	     sweep the gemm ratio is NOT shape-invariant (1.77x vs 2.03x), because it
615	     tracks whether the tensor fits L3.

618	
619	## F9. Q1_0 d4 kernels: kill the vtype churn - DONE 2026-08-01
620	
621	- Status: DONE and shipped in the same Q1_VD4DOT build. Decode 1.26x, prefill
622	  1.14-1.17x on top of F8.
623	- The problem, from the F8 O3 assembly: the kernels alternate between the byte
624	  view (vlm mask load, vmerge sign expand) and the 32-bit view (vmv.v.x
625	  broadcast, the dot). Every alternation needs a vsetvli, which does no
626	  arithmetic. 4 per dot in the gemv - 40% of its inner loop. GCC's share is
627	  that it cannot see inside an inline asm block, so it assumes each one left
628	  vtype unknown and re-issues its own on top of the one in the block.
629	- WHAT DID NOT WORK, worth knowing: grouping the two widths in the SOURCE
630	  (all 4 vlm+vmerge, then all 4 broadcast+dot). The scheduler interleaves them
631	  again and it only got the gemv from 4.00 to 2.00 vsetvli per dot.
632	  What works is putting everything at e32 INSIDE one asm block - the
633	  broadcasts included - so GCC only ever has e8 work to schedule.
634	  Side benefit: taking the activation quads as uint32 GPRs and writing
635	  vmv.v.x by hand makes the vlse32 stride-0 trap impossible by construction,
636	  so q1_bcast_act4 and its barrier are gone.
637	- ALSO DID NOT WORK: 4 scratch activation registers instead of 2, to double
638	  the distance between each vmv.v.x and the dot that consumes it. No spills,
639	  4.06 vs 4.13 instrs/dot - and 855,476 cycles vs 818,314, i.e. 4.5% WORSE.
640	  The producer-consumer distance is not what limits the gemm. Reverted.
641	- STATIC (O3, between the first and last dot):
642	      vsetvli per dot   gemv 4.00 -> 0.94     gemm 2.00 -> 0.52
643	      instrs per dot    gemv 10.00 -> 7.90    gemm 9.00 -> 4.13
644	  The gemm gains more because the smaller body also let GCC unroll its column
645	  loop 8x, which it would not do before. No vector spills in either.
646	- MEASURED, same engine and cmdline as F8:
647	      node                        F8          F9    F9/F8   vs pristine
648	      K=51 decode  nrows=2    457,092     362,799    1.26x    12.34x
649	      K=51 prefill nrows=4    931,754     818,314    1.14x    10.85x
650	      K=56 prefill nrows=4  6,636,852   5,683,029    1.17x        -
651	- THE INTERESTING PART - decode and prefill are now bound by different things.
652	  Cycles per issued instruction (cycles / dots / instrs-per-dot):
653	      gemv   F8 2.23  ->  F9 2.24     unchanged
654	      gemm   F8 2.53  ->  F9 4.84     nearly doubled
655	  The gemv is purely instruction-issue bound: its cost per instruction did not
656	  move, so F9 converted the instruction saving straight into cycles, 1:1. That
657	  also means F8's "instruction-issue floor" of 328,865 (measured with HVM) was
658	  never a floor - it was an instruction count, and F9 beat it at 362,799 with
659	  no HVM at all.
660	  The gemm is NOT issue bound any more. At the gemv's 2.24 cyc/instr its 4.13
661	  instructions per dot should cost ~9.2 cycles; it costs 20.0. So ~11 cycles
662	  per dot are stall, and cutting instructions further will not help prefill.
663	  Both kernels now sit at 17.7 (gemv) and 20.0 (gemm) cycles per
664	  nds.vd4dots.vv, which is suspicious enough to suspect the instruction's own
665	  throughput at e32/m2 - but that is NOT established.
666	  THE EXPERIMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, not yet run: d4-nopf and d4-hvm on the
667	  PREFILL node (both build targets already exist; ~25 min including builds).
668	  If prefetch-off and HVM both leave it near 818,314, the limit is the dot
669	  rate and prefill is done until the ISA changes. If HVM moves it, the limit
670	  is the 4 activation streams plus the weight stream, and the fix is software.
671	- Key files: arch/riscv/repack.cpp `q1_vd4dots_x4_m2` (gemv: 4 pairs into one
672	  accumulator) and `q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2` (gemm: one weight against the 4 rows
673	  of the M-tile). Gate: ./check-vd4dots.sh, VTYPE-CHURN budget of 1 vsetvli
674	  per dot, which fails on the F8 code at O3 and passes now.
675	- Correctness: bit-identical, not just close - test-repack-q1_0 13/13 with
676	  every nmse unchanged from the F8 run, at Q1_VD4DOT=1 and Q1_VD4DOT=0.
677

749	## Parked (27B-only; nothing above depends on this)
750	
751	### F0. qwen35 (hybrid attention) produces garbage on rv64
752	
753	- Status: **FIXED 2026-08-05.** Root cause was not a qwen35 op at all: the
754	  RVV `ggml_vec_dot_f32` (and the zvfh `ggml_vec_dot_f16`) initialized their
755	  accumulator with a `_tu` intrinsic whose merge operand was an
756	  UNINITIALIZED register. That value is indeterminate, so GCC 14.2 (Andes)
757	  was free to re-materialize the init - and did, under whatever vtype was
758	  current: the emitted code zeroed vsum under `e8,m2,ta`, leaving 6 of the 8
759	  accumulator registers tail-agnostic. QEMU implements tail-agnostic as
760	  all-ones, so every dot returned garbage of ~1e19 and the delta-net
761	  recurrence exploded (first divergent node: GATED_DELTA_NET, layer 2,
762	  decode path). qwen3 4B/8B never call vec_dot_f32/f16 on their decode paths
763	  (flash-attn f16 KV is scalar without zvfh; no delta-net), which is why
764	  they were always correct and every recorded cycle number stands.
765	  - Diagnosis: 3-way llama-eval-callback diff (x86 host / rv64 scalar /
766	    rv64 RVV under qemu-user) at 1 token; per-TU -march bisect (ops.cpp
767	    scalar -> still garbage; vec.cpp scalar -> correct); disassembly showed
768	    the double-init; standalone harnesses proved every helper and the
769	    kernel math correct in isolation (the miscompile is
770	    scheduling-context-sensitive).
771	  - Fix: plain (non-_tu) accumulator init at vlmax + plain stripe loads;
772	    `_tu` stays only on the accumulate, which is what preserves high-lane
773	    partials on the final short stripe. Verified: fixed object has a single
774	    correctly-typed init; 27B decode text matches x86 host at temp 0.
775	- Description: Bonsai-27B (arch qwen35, ~75% linear attention) generates
776	  incoherent text on rv64 QEMU while the same GGUF + prompt on x86 host is
777	  correct. 4B/8B (plain qwen3) are coherent on rv64, and test-quantize-fns
778	  passes all 35 quant types under QEMU (Q1_0/Q8_0 kernels exonerated).
779	  Suspect: qwen35-only ops (delta-net / linear-attention recurrence,
780	  gating) in their RVV or fp16 (zvfh) paths, or a shape-dependent kernel
781	  edge case only the 27B tensor sizes hit.
782	- Diagnosis plan when resumed: (1) rebuild rv64 with GGML_RVV=OFF, run 27B
783	  few tokens - scalar correct means an RVV kernel, scalar broken means
784	  generic C or fp16 ABI; (2) bisect op-level with llama-eval-callback host
785	  vs QEMU, find first divergent op; (3) fix + add the failing shape to
786	  test-backend-ops.
787	- Key files: src/models/ (qwen35 graph), ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp, vec.h,
788	  ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/.

793	  for scaling checks, not a primary target.

# RISC-V Kernel Optimization Roadmap (Bonsai-4B Q1_0 / Ternary Q2_0)

Primary model: models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf (572 MB, arch qwen3, 36 layers,
embd 2560, GQA with 1024-wide K/V projections, 253 MUL_MAT nodes per token
= 36 x 7 + lm_head).

Why 4B (decision 2026-07-21, replaces the old 27B focus):
- Fits andesim hybrid's hard 2 GiB guest-RAM cap with room for KV cache and
  compute buffers (27B needs ~4.5 GB - blocked until andesim grows >2 GiB
  DRAM support).
- Plain qwen3: output is coherent on rv64. The qwen35 hybrid-attention bug
  (old F0) only affects 27B, so it no longer blocks anything - parked below.
- The full closed loop already works on 4B: end-to-end cycle-accurate
  per-kernel measurement under andesim hybrid marker mode was confirmed
  2026-07-16 (see Measurement setup).

Hardware targets (both vsim engines, VLEN 512-2048 family per F4 design):
- vsim:ax45mpv_premium - VLEN=512, DLEN=512, ELEN=32, no zfh/zvfh.
- vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 - VLEN=1024, ELEN=64, first engine with real L3.

Baselines:
- QEMU proxy (insn-count, -t 8, build-rv64-noomp, 2026-07-15):
  4B ~19-21 s/token. QEMU time tracks instruction count, not latency.
- Real cycles, hybrid marker ROI at K=51 (layer 7 V projection, 2560x1024,
  the smallest matmul in the model - nothing smaller exists per-layer):
  - ax45mpv_premium: 6528953 cycles (2026-07-16, stable across runs)
  - ax46mpv_fpga_l3: 4476168 cycles (2026-07-16, pristine upstream ggml)
  These are THE per-kernel before/after gate for F1-F7: same K, same model,
  real pipeline + memory system.

Rules for every feature below:
- TDD: first add a correctness test comparing the new kernel against the
  matching *_generic function on random data (test-quantize-fns style),
  see it fail/pass, then optimize. Never commit a kernel without the test.
- Benchmark gate: QEMU proxy for correctness + rough insn counts, then
  hybrid marker ROI cycles before/after (the real number). FPGA only for
  final full-token figures.

ELEN=32 constraint (ax45mpv_premium): no 64-bit vector elements anywhere.
Stock repack.cpp uses __riscv_vsseg4e64 -> GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF today; any
new F4 kernel must stay e32-clean (the Nx1 design already is: vlm masks,
int16 sumi, fp32 accumulators). Also: premium's FP datapath rejects LMUL=8
float ops (integer LMUL=8 is fine) - F4's VLEN=512 -> m4 fp32 mapping is
exactly at the safe limit; never use m8 for float.

Status legend: TODO / IN-PROGRESS / DONE / PARKED

---

## F1. Q1_0 multi-row vec_dot (nrows = 2)

- Status: TODO
- Description: The Q1_0 dot kernel recomputes/reloads the same activations
  for every weight row. Set `.nrows = 2` (later 4) so one call computes 2
  output elements: load + negate activations once, per row only do mask
  load (vlm) + vmerge + reduce. Expected ~1.5-2x on the dominant matmul path.
- Gate: K=51 ROI cycles before/after (V projection is exactly this path).
- Key files:
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484-578 (vl256/vl128 kernels + dispatcher)
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:227-232 (.nrows field of GGML_TYPE_Q1_0)
- Dependencies: none. Small diff, big win - good first step if F4 stalls.

## F2. Q1_0 defer reductions - REMOVED

- Status: REMOVED (2026-07-22, user decision). The vl512/vl512w candidate
  kernels were deleted from kernel-lab/ (q1_0.c/h, test harness); the lab
  dispatcher routes VLEN >= 256 to vl256 again. Rationale: it removed the
  per-group scalar stall but kept the horizontal reduction and the 32-lane
  fill, so it could never be more than a modest win; F4 (row-parallel
  repack) solves the actual problem and makes this path dead weight.
  Lesson kept for the record: QEMU TCG charges per vector instruction and
  makes scalar ops ~free, so this kind of stall-removal restructure READS
  AS A REGRESSION under QEMU (n=8192: vl256 57.5us vs vl512 75.5us) -
  never judge restructures by QEMU; only vsim/FPGA cycles count.

## F3. Q1_0 full-VLEN utilization - FOLDED INTO F1/F4

- Status: folded (2026-07-16 finding) - because Q8_0 activations are NOT
  contiguous (34-byte block stride), filling a 512-bit register costs slide
  instructions that cancel the saved vlm/vneg/vmerge. Wider vl alone cannot
  win for the vec_dot shape; width pays off only via repack (F4, contiguous
  interleaved rows) or multi-row amortization (F1). Not a standalone feature.

## F4. Q1_0 repack, ROW-PARALLEL Nx1 (the wide-VLEN win)

- Status: IN-PROGRESS (2026-07-22) - F4a DONE, F4b lab-verified pending
  cycle gate; largest expected win; supersedes F1-F3 for matmul.
- Core decision (2026-07-20, wide-VLEN analysis): use the ROW-PARALLEL
  `Nx1` layout (blocklen=1, like `ggml_gemv_q4_0_16x1_q8_0_generic`,
  repack.cpp:1370), NOT the `q4_0_8x8` mmla-fold layout. Reason:
  * The 8x8 path uses vwmul/vwmacc + a vnsrl reduction tree (repack.cpp
    arch/riscv:161-177) - the multiplies exist to dequant 4-bit weights,
    and the fold tree is a horizontal reduction that under-uses wide VLEN
    (8 fp32 lanes, so 8/64 = 12% of a VLEN=2048 datapath). F3 already
    proved horizontal reductions are the bottleneck; the fold tree is one.
  * Q1_0 weights are +-1: the multiply collapses to a conditional add, and
    the ONLY reason to reduce (per-32 Q8_0 scale) is handled at group
    boundaries. Row-parallel keeps N rows in N lanes; the K-reduction
    becomes a loop-carried VERTICAL add per lane -> ZERO horizontal
    reductions in the whole kernel. This is the fix for VLEN 512-2048:
    spend LMUL on rows (useful work), not on one row's reduction.
- Layout `block_q1_0_Nx1` (N rows interleaved, per 128-col block, 18N bytes
  = N * sizeof(block_q1_0), same total size):
  * sign planes, column-major: for global col c in 0..127, N bits (one per
    row) -> 16N bytes, loadable as a per-column N-bit mask (vlm).
  * N fp16 weight scales (one d per row per 128-block) -> 2N bytes.
- RVV gemv inner loop (per 128-block, N rows in lanes, no reductions):
  ```
  facc_block[N] = 0                                  // fp32, N lanes
  for g in 0..3:                                     // 4 Q8_0 groups / 128
      dy = fp16_to_fp32(a[g].d)                      // scalar (shared/rows)
      sumi[N] = 0                                    // int16, 32*127<32767 ok
      for c in 0..31:
          y    = a[g].qs[c]                          // scalar int8
          mask = vlm(sign plane col 32*g+c)          // N bits
          sumi = vsub_vx(sumi, y)                    // -y on all lanes
          sumi = vadd_vx_m(mask, sumi, 2*y)          // +2y where bit set => +-y
      facc_block = vfmacc_vf(facc_block, dy, vfcvt(sumi))   // scalar dy
  sumf[N] = vfmacc_vv(sumf, dx[N], facc_block)       // vector weight scale
  // after K loop: store sumf[N] to N contiguous outputs
  ```
  ~3 ops/col (1 vlm + vsub_vx + vadd_vx_m), all N-wide; ~393 N-wide ops per
  block-tile => ~6 ops/row/block at N=64 vs ~20 for single-row vec_dot, AND
  full VLMAX, AND no reduction stalls. Per-column vlm (128/block) is the
  main tuning point. Everything is e8/e16/e32 - ELEN=32-clean by design.

## F6. Q1_0 ACE-RVV custom instruction co-design (COPILOT)

- Status: SUPERSEDED for the gemv path by F8 below - the stock vendor
  instruction turned out to be enough, so no custom ACE silicon is needed to
  get the row-parallel in-lane dot. F6 stays open only as the design study for
  an instruction that goes BEYOND nds.vd4dots (1-bit weight operand, i.e. 8x
  less register traffic than expanding to +-1 int8 - candidate A below).
- Original status: TODO - design fixed 2026-07-20; user confirmed int8
  dot-product HW exists and wants to design custom ACE-RVV instructions (not
  just use stock xandesvdot). Awaiting user pick of candidate A/B/C.
- Toolchain / template: user's ACE lab at
  /local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/ace-tq1 (COPILOT 7.3, AX46MPV,
  vlen=256 sim). unpack.ace already defines: `v_w_mul_free_macc`
  (multiply-free widening MAC, weight in {-1,0,1}: result_2int += act_i8 (*)
  weight_i8, no multiplier) and trit `unpack` insns. tq1.c dataflow =
  unpack -> v_w_mul_free_macc -> ONE vwredsum/256-block -> one scale (works
  because TQ1 pairs with Q8_K = 1 scale/256). Q1_0 pairs with 4x Q8_0 =
  1 scale/32; that mismatch is what the ACE insn must erase.
- Operand model (from unpack.ace): `rvv_insn N { operand = {io|in|out
  vrf:{int|2int|4int|uint} ...}; vector_unit = elen; csim = %{..%};
  latency = 1; }`. vrf:int=i8 lane, 2int/4int=widened i16/i32 result,
  uint=packed bytes. v_q_tq2_unpack already returns 4int (i32) from a packed
  byte -> in-lane widening + reading a packed bit-plane is in-idiom.
- Candidates (precise I/O):
  * A. `v_q1_rowdot` - ROW-PARALLEL K-way sign-dot, THE wide-VLEN optimum.
    Pairs with F4 Nx1 repack: lanes = rows, activation broadcast (splat like
    the q4_0_8x8 vmv_v_x_i64 trick), each lane holds one row's sign bits;
    in-lane 4-way sign-dot, accumulate per row. NO reduction, full VLEN.
      rvv_insn v_q1_rowdot {   // result[lane] += sum_{i<4}(bit_i? +act_i : -act_i)
        operand = { io vrf:4int result, in vrf:int activation, in vrf:uint signbits };
        vector_unit = elen; latency = 1; }
    Sign-bit analog of NDS.VD4DOTS but weight stays 1-bit (8x less reg
    traffic) and the multiplier is just a conditional-negate add-tree
    (cheaper HW than v_w_mul_free_macc). RECOMMENDED.
  * C. `v_q1_sign_macc` - fused single-row (stays in vec_dot shape). Element-
    wise; still needs the per-32 vwredsum tail.
      rvv_insn v_q1_sign_macc {   // result[j] += (bit_j? +act[j] : -act[j])
        operand = { io vrf:2int result, in vrf:int activation, in vrf:uint signbits };
        vector_unit = elen; latency = 1; }
  * B. `v_q1_unpack` - minimal: bits -> +-1 int8 (mirror v_q_tq2_unpack),
    then reuse existing v_w_mul_free_macc + vwredsum. Smallest new HW.
- Decision (defaults if user stays away): pick A. Even the TQ1 one-reduce-
  per-block under-fills a wide register (128/1024 lanes at VLEN=2048); only
  row-parallel turns those lanes into output rows and removes the reduction.
  A shares F4's exact Nx1 layout, so base-RVV (F4b) and ACE (this) run on
  the same repacked weights -> direct vsim A/B shootout.
- Activation format: keep per-32 Q8_0 for path A (row-parallel applies the 4
  per-32 scales as 4 vector FMAs, still zero reduction, no accuracy loss).
  Only paths B/C benefit from coarsening to 1 scale/128 (Q8_K-style, matches

  precision, needs a perplexity check.
