## F7. zicbop prefetch of next block - DONE 2026-07-27 (no HVM)

- Status: DONE. Pure-software win, no HVM. This is the path taken after the
  user dropped HVM (HVM maxes at 256 MiB address space and could hold only
  ~1.4% of the 560 MB Q1_0 weights at the fpga_l3 8 MiB size, so it does not
  generalize; software prefetch helps EVERY Q1_0 matmul).
- Why it works: the row-parallel gemv streams `block_q1_0x64` sequentially
  (`bx[l]`, 2176 B = 34 cache lines each). This core's HW prefetcher is shallow
  (`NDS_L3C_PFP_LINE_NUM=0`, D$ 4 entries), so it cannot run far enough ahead
  to hide the L3/DRAM miss latency that makes the repacked kernel load-bound.
  A `__builtin_prefetch` of the block `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST` ahead pulls it in
  early.
- CORRECTION to the old note: the march did NOT already include zicbop - it is
  behind the `GGML_RV_ZICBOP` CMake option (off by default), and without it
  `__builtin_prefetch` compiles to a nop. Build must pass `-DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON`
  (added to build.sh; gcc 14.2 then emits real `prefetch.r`).
- Measured (K=51 ROI, fpga_l3 VLEN 1024, cycle-accurate vsim). Prefetch
  distance sweep (ALL rows already use repack; DIST=0 = prefetch off):
    DIST=0 (baseline repack)  2,144,213
    DIST=1                    1,391,650   1.54x   <- BEST, shipped default
    DIST=2                    1,430,534   1.50x
    DIST=4                    1,506,429   1.42x
  More lookahead is worse - one 34-line block ahead already covers the latency;
  further only adds MSHR/cache pressure.
- Stacked vs the ORIGINAL kernel (no repack, upstream per-row vec_dot with the
  per-32 vwredsum reduction):
    original (no repack)            4,476,168   1.00x
    repack (F4)                     2,144,213   2.09x
    repack + prefetch DIST=1 (F7)   1,391,650   3.22x
  The two wins are independent and stack: repack fixes the compute (no idle
  lanes at wide VLEN), prefetch fixes the memory (weight stream no longer
  stalls on L3/DRAM misses).
- Correctness: bit-identical text vs baseline (andesim --mode fast, greedy),
  and `prefetch.r` is architecturally a no-op hint (no reg/mem write, no fault).
- Key files:
  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp: helper `q1_prefetch_block` +
    one call at the top of each gemv l-loop; `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST` macro
    (default 1, override at build time).
  - build.sh: `-DGGML_RV_ZICBOP=ON`.
- GEMM (prefill) path prefetched too (same helper in both `q1_gemm_64x1_*`
  l-loops), but the win is marginal: on a PURE-gemm node (nrows=4, one M-tile,
  no gemv remainder) 1,696,704 -> 1,649,275 = **1.03x**. Reason: gemm loads
  each weight block once and reuses it across the M-tile of 4 activations, so
  it is ~4x less memory-bound than gemv (which streams the weight per single

## F8. Q1_0 gemv + gemm on nds.vd4dots.vv (XAndesVDot) - DONE 2026-07-31

- Status: DONE. gemv/decode 2026-07-29, gemm/prefill 2026-07-31.
- Premise correction that unblocked it: `nds.vd4dots.vv` is a STOCK Andes
  vendor instruction, not custom ACE. It is already in the RTL of all three
  vsim engines (`NDS_VECTOR_VDOT_SUPPORT {yes}` in ax46mpv_fpga_l3.cfg,
  ax45mpv_premium*.cfg), in the ast542 Linux toolchain's assembler
  (`-march=..._xandesvdot`), and in the andesim fast leg (the engine's
  `-readconfig` qemu cfg sets MMSC_CFG.VDOT even though qemu's own
  andes-ax46mpv default does not - verified with a freestanding probe).
  So F6's "needs COPILOT first" premise was wrong for Strategy B.
- Semantics (verified by running): with vtype e32,
  `vd[lane] += sum_{k<4} vs1[4*lane+k] * vs2[4*lane+k]`, int8 x int8 into the
  i32 lane, src and dst at the SAME LMUL. GCC 14.2 has no intrinsic -> inline
  asm; safe because GCC treats an asm block as a vtype killer and re-emits its
  own vsetvli after it.
- What changed vs F4/F7. The kernel is the same row-parallel 64x1 gemv; only
  the K-reduction moves into the instruction:
    F4/F7 per 1 column : vlm(8B) + vsub.vx + vadd.vx,mu   = 3 m1 ops
    F8    per 4 columns: vlm(32B) + vmv.v.x + vmerge.vim + nds.vd4dots.vv
                                                          = 4 m2 ops
  At VLEN=1024, e32/m2 is exactly 64 i32 lanes = the 64 rows, and the same
  register group seen as i8 is 256 bytes = 64 rows x 4 columns - the operand
  shape the instruction wants. Int sums land in i32 instead of i16, converted
  to float at the same place, so results are BIT-IDENTICAL to F7.
- Layout: `Q1_VD4DOT=1` flips the sign-plane order to 4 columns per lane
  (bit `4*j + c%4` of plane `c/4`). Same block, same size. The repack writer
  and both generic readers share ONE helper, `q1_0x64_sign_bit` in repack.h,
  so the orders cannot drift apart. It is a whole-binary switch, not a
  kernel-only one - hence a separate `bash build.sh d4` artifact.
- MEASURED, K=51 ROI (blk.7.attn_v [2560 x 1024], nrows=2 gemv), andesim
  hybrid marker mode, vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3, same cmdline as every other gate:

    repack (F4)                      2,144,213   2.09x
    repack + prefetch (F7, shipped)  1,389,236   3.22x
    + nds.vd4dots (F8)                 457,092   9.79x   <- 3.04x over F7

  range of node sizes. CROSS-CHECK: this sweep's prefetch-vs-pristine per-layer
  figure is 178,647,490/52,752,463 = 3.386x, which reproduces the 3.39x the
  independent F7 sweep measured - the two sessions agree.
  ffn_down is the outlier in BOTH directions: prefetch helps it most (3.77x vs
  ~3.25x elsewhere) and d4 adds the least on top (3.03x), for a combined best-
  in-sweep 11.45x. Its K=9728 is the longest reduction dimension, which is what
  punishes pristine's per-32-column horizontal reduction hardest.
  MEASUREMENT NOTE: measure.sh's default 4h per-leg timeout is NOT enough for
  pristine ffn_down (49.0M cycles, ~3.9h) - the first attempt died with exit 1
  and an empty grep. Use TIMEOUT=28800000 for that leg.
- GEMM / PREFILL (2026-07-31). Same instruction, same weight stream; the only
  new problem is the activation side. The x4 activation block stores
  qs[c*4 + m] (blck_size_interleave 1) but the dot wants row m's columns
  c..c+3 as ONE 32-bit element - a stride-4 gather. De-interleave the whole
  row tile once up front instead: read the block as 32 u32 elements and peel
  the four byte lanes apart with vnsrl (u32 -> 2x u16 -> 4x u8), 6 shifts + 4
  stores per 32 columns, reused by every column tile. Under 1% of the inner
  loop, and unlike vlse8 or a segment load it is plain RVV that cannot turn
  element-serial. The u32 view is legal because block_q8_0x4 keeps qs 4-byte
  aligned (d[4] is 8 B, sizeof 136) - the opposite of trap 2 below.
  Register budget at e32/m2 forces one change: 4 sumf + 4 acc + dx + w + a +
  vneg1 is already 24 of 32 vector registers, so the per-block float
  accumulator of every other kernel does not fit. Fold the activation scale
  into dx instead, one vfmul per group, same sum:
    sum_l dx * (sum_k da[k]*acc[k])  ==  sum_l sum_k (dx*da[k]) * acc[k]
  MEASURED, prefill nodes (nrows=4, pure gemm; `PROMPT="The capital of France"
  WARMUP=--no-warmup bash measure.sh ...`), same engine as everything above:
      K  node       shape        pristine     prefetch          d4  d4/pf  d4/pri
      51 attn_v     2560x1024   8,875,248    1,651,949     931,754  1.77x   9.52x
      56 ffn_down   9728x2560           -   13,474,132   6,636,852  2.03x       -
  (the prefetch leg reproduces the earlier session's 1,649,275 to 0.16%, so
  the columns are directly comparable; pristine ffn_down was not run - at
  ~0.98 cyc/MAC it is a ~9 h leg and adds nothing the gemv sweep did not.)
- WHY PREFILL GAINS LESS THAN DECODE (1.77x vs 3.04x on the same node). The
  two paths converge on the same floor - look at cycles per multiply-add:
                          decode (gemv, nrows=2)   prefill (gemm, nrows=4)
      repack + prefetch          0.2650                  0.1576   (1.68x better)
      + nds.vd4dots              0.0872                  0.0889   (1.00x - same)
  F7's gemm was already 1.68x more efficient per MAC than its gemv, because
  reusing each weight block across 4 rows hid the memory stall. The d4 kernel
  has no stall left to hide on this node, so that advantage evaporates and
  prefill/decode cost the same per MAC. Prefill's smaller headline ratio is
  not a weaker kernel, it is a better starting point.
  ffn_down is the exception that confirms the mechanism: at 3.5 MB it does NOT
  fit fpga_l3's 2 MB L3, so weight reuse still buys real memory traffic there
  and the d4 gemm IS 1.29x better per MAC than the d4 gemv (0.0666 vs 0.0860)
  - which is why its d4/prefetch is 2.03x instead of 1.77x. Same conclusion as
  the HVM caveat below: memory still matters, but only above the L3 size.
- COMPUTE / MEMORY SPLIT after F8 (K=51 attn_v, same engine; the number to
  plan hardware against). Two extra legs, `bash build.sh d4-nopf` and
  `bash build.sh d4-hvm`:
      d4, prefetch OFF                 588,771
      d4 + prefetch (shipped d4)       457,092
      d4 + prefetch + weights in HVM   328,865   <- 1.39x over d4+prefetch
                                                    13.61x over pristine
  HVM removes essentially all memory wait, so 328,865 is the INSTRUCTION-ISSUE
  FLOOR (~92K instructions -> 3.6 cyc/instr, which is about the m2-at-DLEN-1024
  issue limit). That splits d4+prefetch into:
      328,865 (72%) instruction issue - no memory fix can touch this
      128,227 (28%) residual memory stall
  and splits the total stall of the un-prefetched kernel almost exactly in half:
  prefetch hides 131,679 (51%), HVM the other 128,227 (49%).
  PLANNING CONSEQUENCE: the big remaining pot is compute, not memory. F6-A
  (1-bit weight operand: drops the vmerge AND cuts weight register traffic 8x)
  attacks the 72%; HVM attacks the 28%. They do not overlap, so they stack -
  a 2x on compute plus HVM would be ~2.8x on top of today.
  CAVEAT that cuts the other way: attn_v's 360 KB working set FITS fpga_l3's
  2 MB L3. A 27B ffn_down is 12 MB per tensor, where L3 is useless, so the
  memory fraction there should be well above 28% and HVM worth more than
  1.39x. Measuring d4-hvm on K=56 (ffn_down, the largest node) would give the
  "memory fraction vs node size" curve that a big-local-memory decision needs.
- TWO TRAPS, both cost real time, both are in the code as comments:
  1. `vlse32.v vd,(rs1),zero` (stride-0 broadcast) is element-serial on this
     core - 18x slower in the lab. GCC contracts "load a word, splat it" into
     exactly that, and it did so again inside ggml. Fix: pin the word in a GPR
     with an empty asm barrier first (`q1_bcast_act4`), so it stays lw+vmv.v.x.
     Gate it by disassembling: the gemv kernel must show 8 vmv.v.x, 0 vlse32.
  2. The core faults on a MISALIGNED 32-bit vector element load, and
     `block_q8_0` puts qs at struct offset 2, so every other q8 group is 2 mod
     4. Fix: restage the activation quants once per gemv call into an alloca'd
     buffer via vector BYTE ld/st (no alignment rule at EEW=8). Amortized over
     the nc/64 row tiles it is ~0.4% of the kernel.
- Correctness, three levels:
  1. Unit: tests/test-repack-q1_0.cpp at VLEN=1024, 13/13 nmse < 1e-14 vs the
     default-buft reference (0.000e+00 on every gemv case - the gemm cases sit

     the pure-gemm case already at nmse=0, which is what proved the layout

     M=4 puts a structured sign pattern through it.
     TEETH, verified not assumed: swapping two rows inside the gemm
     de-interleave gives 11/13, failing exactly the two gemm cases and nothing
     else. Note what this implies - RANDOM weights cannot tell you WHICH
     permutation the repack produced, and the generic C path can never
     validate layout at all, because writer and reader share the same helper
     so any error cancels. Only the RVV kernels bake the order into the
     vlm/vmerge/vd4dots operand shape.
  2. Codegen: ./check-vd4dots.sh, at O2/O3/Os. Per KERNEL (the vd4dot kernels stay

  3. End to end: andesim --mode fast, greedy, Bonsai-4B - d4 and the shipped

  - ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp: repack writer + both generic readers use it

- Next levers, in order of expected value:
  1. F9, vtype churn - DONE 2026-08-01, see below. Was: measured from the O3
     assembly, per nds.vd4dots issued:
       gemv  80 instrs / 8 dots = 10.0, of which 4.0 are vsetvli (40%)
       gemm  36 instrs / 4 dots =  9.0, of which 2.5 are vsetvli (28%)
     CAUSE, and it is NOT mainly the inline asm - it is e8/e32 ping-pong. One
     real gemv column at O3:
       vlm.v v0,0(t0)            # mask                          e8
       lw t0,4(t5)
       vsetvli zero,a4,e32,m2                                #  -> e32
       vmv.v.x v16,t0            # broadcast 4 activations
       vsetvli zero,a5,e8,m2                                 #  -> e8
       vmerge.vim v10,v4,1,v0    # mask -> +-1 bytes
       vsetvli t0,zero,e32,m2    # (inside the asm)          #  -> e32
       nds.vd4dots.vv v2,v10,v16 # the only real work
       addi t0,a6,64
       vsetvli zero,a5,e8,m2                                 #  -> e8, next vlm
     Ten instructions, one of which multiplies. The work genuinely alternates
     between the byte view (mask, merge) and the 32-bit view (broadcast, dot),
     and each alternation costs one vsetvli; GCC re-emitting after the asm
     (because it cannot see the asm left vtype at e32/m2) is only ONE of the
     four. So widening the asm block alone recovers 1 of 4, not 4 of 4.
     FIX: batch by element width, not by column - do 4 columns of e8 work
     under one vsetvli, then 4 columns of e32 work under one more, with the 4
     dots in a single asm block. 4 dots go from 40 instrs / 16 vsetvli to ~26
     / 2, about 1.5x on the gemv. Register cost there is mild (4 live weight
     vectors = 8 of 32, and the gemv tracks one output row), so it fits; the
     gemm is tighter (4 sumf + 4 acc = 16 already) and may only batch 2.
     CAVEAT: this is an instruction count, not cycles. vsetvli is cheap, so
     expect less than the ratio suggests. Nothing built or measured yet.

     sweep the gemm ratio is NOT shape-invariant (1.77x vs 2.03x), because it
     tracks whether the tensor fits L3.

---

## F9. Q1_0 d4 kernels: kill the vtype churn - DONE 2026-08-01

- Status: DONE and shipped in the same Q1_VD4DOT build. Decode 1.26x, prefill
  1.14-1.17x on top of F8.
- The problem, from the F8 O3 assembly: the kernels alternate between the byte
  view (vlm mask load, vmerge sign expand) and the 32-bit view (vmv.v.x
  broadcast, the dot). Every alternation needs a vsetvli, which does no
  arithmetic. 4 per dot in the gemv - 40% of its inner loop. GCC's share is
  that it cannot see inside an inline asm block, so it assumes each one left
  vtype unknown and re-issues its own on top of the one in the block.
- WHAT DID NOT WORK, worth knowing: grouping the two widths in the SOURCE
  (all 4 vlm+vmerge, then all 4 broadcast+dot). The scheduler interleaves them
  again and it only got the gemv from 4.00 to 2.00 vsetvli per dot.
  What works is putting everything at e32 INSIDE one asm block - the
  broadcasts included - so GCC only ever has e8 work to schedule.
  Side benefit: taking the activation quads as uint32 GPRs and writing
  vmv.v.x by hand makes the vlse32 stride-0 trap impossible by construction,
  so q1_bcast_act4 and its barrier are gone.
- ALSO DID NOT WORK: 4 scratch activation registers instead of 2, to double
  the distance between each vmv.v.x and the dot that consumes it. No spills,
  4.06 vs 4.13 instrs/dot - and 855,476 cycles vs 818,314, i.e. 4.5% WORSE.
  The producer-consumer distance is not what limits the gemm. Reverted.
- STATIC (O3, between the first and last dot):
      vsetvli per dot   gemv 4.00 -> 0.94     gemm 2.00 -> 0.52
      instrs per dot    gemv 10.00 -> 7.90    gemm 9.00 -> 4.13
  The gemm gains more because the smaller body also let GCC unroll its column
  loop 8x, which it would not do before. No vector spills in either.
- MEASURED, same engine and cmdline as F8:
      node                        F8          F9    F9/F8   vs pristine
      K=51 decode  nrows=2    457,092     362,799    1.26x    12.34x
      K=51 prefill nrows=4    931,754     818,314    1.14x    10.85x
      K=56 prefill nrows=4  6,636,852   5,683,029    1.17x        -
- THE INTERESTING PART - decode and prefill are now bound by different things.
  Cycles per issued instruction (cycles / dots / instrs-per-dot):
      gemv   F8 2.23  ->  F9 2.24     unchanged
      gemm   F8 2.53  ->  F9 4.84     nearly doubled
  The gemv is purely instruction-issue bound: its cost per instruction did not
  move, so F9 converted the instruction saving straight into cycles, 1:1. That
  also means F8's "instruction-issue floor" of 328,865 (measured with HVM) was
  never a floor - it was an instruction count, and F9 beat it at 362,799 with
  no HVM at all.
  The gemm is NOT issue bound any more. At the gemv's 2.24 cyc/instr its 4.13
  instructions per dot should cost ~9.2 cycles; it costs 20.0. So ~11 cycles
  per dot are stall, and cutting instructions further will not help prefill.
  Both kernels now sit at 17.7 (gemv) and 20.0 (gemm) cycles per
  nds.vd4dots.vv, which is suspicious enough to suspect the instruction's own
  throughput at e32/m2 - but that is NOT established.
  THE EXPERIMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, not yet run: d4-nopf and d4-hvm on the
  PREFILL node (both build targets already exist; ~25 min including builds).
  If prefetch-off and HVM both leave it near 818,314, the limit is the dot
  rate and prefill is done until the ISA changes. If HVM moves it, the limit
  is the 4 activation streams plus the weight stream, and the fix is software.
- Key files: arch/riscv/repack.cpp `q1_vd4dots_x4_m2` (gemv: 4 pairs into one
  accumulator) and `q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2` (gemm: one weight against the 4 rows
  of the M-tile). Gate: ./check-vd4dots.sh, VTYPE-CHURN budget of 1 vsetvli
  per dot, which fails on the F8 code at O3 and passes now.
- Correctness: bit-identical, not just close - test-repack-q1_0 13/13 with
  every nmse unchanged from the F8 run, at Q1_VD4DOT=1 and Q1_VD4DOT=0.

## Parked (27B-only; nothing above depends on this)

### F0. qwen35 (hybrid attention) produces garbage on rv64

- Status: **FIXED 2026-08-05.** Root cause was not a qwen35 op at all: the
  RVV `ggml_vec_dot_f32` (and the zvfh `ggml_vec_dot_f16`) initialized their
  accumulator with a `_tu` intrinsic whose merge operand was an
  UNINITIALIZED register. That value is indeterminate, so GCC 14.2 (Andes)
  was free to re-materialize the init - and did, under whatever vtype was
  current: the emitted code zeroed vsum under `e8,m2,ta`, leaving 6 of the 8
  accumulator registers tail-agnostic. QEMU implements tail-agnostic as
  all-ones, so every dot returned garbage of ~1e19 and the delta-net
  recurrence exploded (first divergent node: GATED_DELTA_NET, layer 2,
  decode path). qwen3 4B/8B never call vec_dot_f32/f16 on their decode paths
  (flash-attn f16 KV is scalar without zvfh; no delta-net), which is why
  they were always correct and every recorded cycle number stands.
  - Diagnosis: 3-way llama-eval-callback diff (x86 host / rv64 scalar /
    rv64 RVV under qemu-user) at 1 token; per-TU -march bisect (ops.cpp
    scalar -> still garbage; vec.cpp scalar -> correct); disassembly showed
    the double-init; standalone harnesses proved every helper and the
    kernel math correct in isolation (the miscompile is
    scheduling-context-sensitive).
  - Fix: plain (non-_tu) accumulator init at vlmax + plain stripe loads;
    `_tu` stays only on the accumulate, which is what preserves high-lane
    partials on the final short stripe. Verified: fixed object has a single
    correctly-typed init; 27B decode text matches x86 host at temp 0.
- Description: Bonsai-27B (arch qwen35, ~75% linear attention) generates
  incoherent text on rv64 QEMU while the same GGUF + prompt on x86 host is
  correct. 4B/8B (plain qwen3) are coherent on rv64, and test-quantize-fns
  passes all 35 quant types under QEMU (Q1_0/Q8_0 kernels exonerated).
  Suspect: qwen35-only ops (delta-net / linear-attention recurrence,
  gating) in their RVV or fp16 (zvfh) paths, or a shape-dependent kernel
  edge case only the 27B tensor sizes hit.
- Diagnosis plan when resumed: (1) rebuild rv64 with GGML_RVV=OFF, run 27B
  few tokens - scalar correct means an RVV kernel, scalar broken means
  generic C or fp16 ABI; (2) bisect op-level with llama-eval-callback host
  vs QEMU, find first divergent op; (3) fix + add the failing shape to
  test-backend-ops.
- Key files: src/models/ (qwen35 graph), ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp, vec.h,
  ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/.

- models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf (QEMU proxy ~124 s/token) - blocked on F0 +

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the confirmed llama.cpp hybrid example from docs/llama_roi_howto.md
# (section 5): layer 7's V projection (K=51) on vsim:ax45mpv_premium.
# Expected: [andesim] 6528953 cycles, ~13 min wall clock.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh            # run (uses existing build)
#   BUILD=1 scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh    # reconfigure + rebuild, then run
#   ROI_K=52 BUILD=1 scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh   # retarget the measured node
set -euo pipefail

ANDESIM_DIR="${ANDESIM_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)}"
LLAMA_DIR="${LLAMA_DIR:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}"
BUILD_DIR="$LLAMA_DIR/build-rv64-static"
MODEL="${MODEL:-$LLAMA_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}"
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"
ROI_K="${ROI_K:-51}"
KANATA="${KANATA:-}"   # set to a path to also dump a Kanata pipeline trace

if [[ "${BUILD:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
    FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K -I $ANDESIM_DIR/build/runtime/include"
    cmake -B "$BUILD_DIR" -S "$LLAMA_DIR" \
        -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
        -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
        -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$FLAGS" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$FLAGS"
    cmake --build "$BUILD_DIR" -j --target llama-completion
    # doc section 3: confirm the .o really carries the intended K
    python3 -c "
import json
for e in json.load(open('$BUILD_DIR/compile_commands.json')):
    if e['file'].endswith('ggml-cpu.c'):
        print(e['command']); break
" | grep -o "ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=$ROI_K" \
        || { echo "ERROR: ggml-cpu.c not configured with K=$ROI_K" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

[[ -x "$BUILD_DIR/bin/llama-completion" ]] \
    || { echo "ERROR: $BUILD_DIR/bin/llama-completion missing; rerun with BUILD=1" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ -f "$MODEL" ]] || { echo "ERROR: model $MODEL missing" >&2; exit 1; }

extra=()
[[ -n "$KANATA" ]] && extra+=(--kanata "$KANATA")

cd "$ANDESIM_DIR"
exec ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
    --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
    "${extra[@]}" \
    "$BUILD_DIR/bin/llama-completion" \
    -- -m "$MODEL" -no-cnv \
       --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cycle sweep over the whole (build variant x MUL_MAT node) grid, in parallel.
#
# measure.sh runs ONE node across a few variants, serially, straight to the
# terminal. This runs the grid: every variant against every node, many legs at
# once, one log per leg, so a killed or timed-out leg is re-run on its own
# without repeating the rest. The deliverable is the table --report prints.
#
#   bash sweep.sh                      # gemm/prefill, K=50..56, all 4 variants
#   MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh            # the decode path instead
#   NODES="51 56" VARIANTS="prefetch d4" bash sweep.sh
#   J=4 bash sweep.sh                  # 4 legs at a time (default 8)
#   bash sweep.sh --report             # re-print the table, run nothing
#   bash sweep.sh --selfcheck          # gate: reproduce two published numbers
#
# MODE picks the ggml path by picking the prompt, which is the ONLY thing that
# decides it (opt_roadmap F7, "MEASUREMENT GOTCHA"):
#   gemv  the warmup forward pass          -> nrows=2, decode kernel
#   gemm  --no-warmup + a 4-token prompt   -> nrows=4, pure prefill, no gemv tail
# The [roi] line reports nrows, and a leg whose nrows disagrees with MODE is
# recorded as BAD-NROWS instead of as a number. This matters more than it
# looks: the wrong prompt measures the OTHER kernel and still prints a
# perfectly plausible cycle count, so the count alone can never catch it.
#
# Concurrency is safe: each hybrid run stages into its own make_temp_dir
# (andesim driver/manifest.cpp), and the cycle figure comes from a
# cycle-accurate RTL model, so host load cannot move it. --selfcheck proves
# both claims at once by running two legs together and comparing each against
# its published value.
#
# Slow: the RTL leg runs at a few kHz. A leg costs about 1 hour per 12M cycles,
# so the pristine ffn_* prefill legs are ~8 h each. Everything else is minutes.
set -u
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
MODEL=${MODEL:-$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}
ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
MODE=${MODE:-gemm}
NODES=${NODES:-"50 51 52 53 54 55 56"}
VARIANTS=${VARIANTS:-"pristine baseline prefetch d4"}
J=${J:-8}
TIMEOUT=${TIMEOUT:-43200000}    # hybrid per-leg spawn timeout, ms (12 h)
OUT=${OUT:-$LLAMA/sweep-$MODE}

case "$MODE" in
  gemm) PROMPT="The capital of France"; WARMUP="--no-warmup"; WANT_NROWS=4 ;;
  gemv) PROMPT="The capital of France is"; WARMUP="";         WANT_NROWS=2 ;;
  *) echo "MODE must be gemm or gemv (got '$MODE')" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

bin_of() {  # $1 variant  $2 node -> the binary build.sh produced for that pair
  local suf=""; [ "$2" = 51 ] || suf="-k$2"
  printf '%s/bin-%s%s\n' "$LLAMA" "$1" "$suf"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- one leg ---
# Runs to completion, leaves everything in the log. Never parses; --report is
# the single parser, so a leg re-run and a fresh report cannot disagree.
run_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
  local v=$1 k=$2 log="$OUT/$v-k$k.log" bin
  bin=$(bin_of "$v" "$k")
  if [ ! -x "$bin" ]; then
    echo "SKIP $v k=$k: no $bin (run: ROI_K=$k bash build.sh $v)" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  # Resume: a leg that already produced both lines is done. Anything else
  # (empty, truncated, timed out) is re-run.
  if [ -f "$log" ] && grep -q '^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" && grep -q '\[roi\] MUL_MAT' "$log"; then
    echo "have $v k=$k"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "run  $v k=$k -> $log"
  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
      --mem-size 2000M --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms "$TIMEOUT" \
      "$bin" -- -m "$MODEL" -no-cnv $WARMUP --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 ) > "$log" 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  grep -E '\[roi\] MUL_MAT|^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" | sed "s/^/    $v k=$k: /"
  [ $rc -eq 0 ] || echo "    $v k=$k: exit $rc" >&2
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- reporting ---
# One log -> "cycles<TAB>nrows<TAB>tensor<TAB>shape", or a reason it is not a
# number. Kept in awk so the nrows gate and the cycle read come from the same
# pass over the same file.
read_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
  local log="$OUT/$1-k$2.log"
  [ -f "$log" ] || { printf 'MISSING\t\t\t\n'; return; }
  awk -v want="$WANT_NROWS" '
    /\[roi\] MUL_MAT/ {
      for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
        if ($i ~ /^src0=/)  { name = substr($i, 6) }
        if ($i ~ /^nrows=/) { nrows = substr($i, 7) }
        if ($i == "[")      { shape = $(i+1) "x" $(i+3) }
      }
    }
    /^\[andesim\] .* cycles/ { cyc = $2 }
    END {
      if (cyc == "")           { printf "PENDING\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
      if (nrows != want)       { printf "BAD-NROWS\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
      printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", cyc, nrows, name, shape
    }' "$log"
}

report() {
  printf '%s sweep -- %s, %s, nrows=%s\n\n' "$MODE" "$(basename "$MODEL")" "$ENGINE" "$WANT_NROWS"
  # Header is built from VARIANTS so a partial sweep still lines up.
  printf '%-4s %-16s %-12s' K tensor shape
  for v in $VARIANTS; do printf ' %14s' "$v"; done
  printf '\n'
  for k in $NODES; do
    local name="" shape="" cells=() f
    for v in $VARIANTS; do
      IFS=$'\t' read -r cyc nrows nm sh <<<"$(read_leg "$v" "$k")"
      [ -n "$nm" ] && name=$nm && shape=$sh
      cells+=("$cyc")
    done
    printf '%-4s %-16s %-12s' "$k" "${name%.weight}" "$shape"
    for f in "${cells[@]}"; do printf ' %14s' "$f"; done
    printf '\n'
  done
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- selfcheck ---
# The harness gate. Two legs with values published in opt_roadmap (F8 for the
# prefetch build, F9 for the vd4dot one), run AT THE SAME TIME. Passing means
# the invocation measures what it claims AND that two concurrent hybrid runs
# do not disturb each other -- which is what licenses the parallel sweep.
selfcheck() {
  [ "$MODE" = gemm ] || { echo "--selfcheck has reference values for MODE=gemm only" >&2; exit 2; }
  mkdir -p "$OUT"
  run_leg prefetch 51 & local p1=$!
  run_leg d4       51 & local p2=$!
  wait $p1 $p2
  local rc=0 got
  # opt_roadmap F8: prefill K=51 prefetch 1,651,949 (an earlier session read
  # 1,649,275 on the same build -- 0.16% apart, so allow 1%).
  # opt_roadmap F9: prefill K=51 d4 818,314.
  for pair in "prefetch:1651949" "d4:818314"; do
    got=$(read_leg "${pair%%:*}" 51 | cut -f1)
    local want=${pair##*:}
    if [[ "$got" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && awk -v g="$got" -v w="$want" 'BEGIN{exit !(g>w*0.99 && g<w*1.01)}'; then
      printf 'PASS %-8s k=51 %s cycles (published %s)\n' "${pair%%:*}" "$got" "$want"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %-8s k=51 got %s, published %s\n' "${pair%%:*}" "$got" "$want"
      rc=1
    fi
  done
  return $rc
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------- main ---
case "${1:-}" in
  --report)    report; exit 0 ;;
  --selfcheck) selfcheck; exit $? ;;
  --leg)       run_leg "$2" "$3"; exit $? ;;   # internal: one xargs slot
esac

[ -f "$MODEL" ] || { echo "no such model: $MODEL" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$OUT"
for k in $NODES; do for v in $VARIANTS; do echo "$v $k"; done; done \
  | xargs -P "$J" -n 2 "$0" --leg
echo
report

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cycle sweep over the whole (build variant x MUL_MAT node) grid, in parallel.
#
# measure.sh runs ONE node across a few variants, serially, straight to the
# terminal. This runs the grid: every variant against every node, many legs at
# once, one log per leg, so a killed or timed-out leg is re-run on its own
# without repeating the rest. The deliverable is the table --report prints.
#
#   bash sweep.sh                      # gemm/prefill, K=50..56, all 4 variants
#   MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh            # the decode path instead
#   NODES="51 56" VARIANTS="prefetch d4" bash sweep.sh
#   J=4 bash sweep.sh                  # 4 legs at a time (default 8)
#   bash sweep.sh --report             # re-print the table, run nothing
#   bash sweep.sh --selfcheck          # gate: reproduce two published numbers
#
# MODE picks the ggml path by picking the prompt, which is the ONLY thing that
# decides it (opt_roadmap F7, "MEASUREMENT GOTCHA"):
#   gemv  the warmup forward pass          -> nrows=2, decode kernel
#   gemm  --no-warmup + a 4-token prompt   -> nrows=4, pure prefill, no gemv tail
# The [roi] line reports nrows, and a leg whose nrows disagrees with MODE is
# recorded as BAD-NROWS instead of as a number. This matters more than it
# looks: the wrong prompt measures the OTHER kernel and still prints a
# perfectly plausible cycle count, so the count alone can never catch it.
#
# Concurrency is safe: each hybrid run stages into its own make_temp_dir
# (andesim driver/manifest.cpp), and the cycle figure comes from a
# cycle-accurate RTL model, so host load cannot move it. --selfcheck proves
# both claims at once by running two legs together and comparing each against
# its published value.
#
# Slow: the RTL leg runs at a few kHz. A leg costs about 1 hour per 12M cycles,
# so the pristine ffn_* prefill legs are ~8 h each. Everything else is minutes.
set -u
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
MODEL=${MODEL:-$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}
ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
MODE=${MODE:-gemm}
NODES=${NODES:-"50 51 52 53 54 55 56"}
VARIANTS=${VARIANTS:-"pristine baseline prefetch d4"}
J=${J:-8}
TIMEOUT=${TIMEOUT:-43200000}    # hybrid per-leg spawn timeout, ms (12 h)
OUT=${OUT:-$LLAMA/sweep-$MODE}

case "$MODE" in
  gemm) PROMPT="The capital of France"; WARMUP="--no-warmup"; WANT_NROWS=4 ;;
  gemv) PROMPT="The capital of France is"; WARMUP="";         WANT_NROWS=2 ;;
  *) echo "MODE must be gemm or gemv (got '$MODE')" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

bin_of() {  # $1 variant  $2 node -> the binary build.sh produced for that pair
  local suf=""; [ "$2" = 51 ] || suf="-k$2"
  printf '%s/bin-%s%s\n' "$LLAMA" "$1" "$suf"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- one leg ---
# Runs to completion, leaves everything in the log. Never parses; --report is
# the single parser, so a leg re-run and a fresh report cannot disagree.
run_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
  local v=$1 k=$2 log="$OUT/$v-k$k.log" bin
  bin=$(bin_of "$v" "$k")
  if [ ! -x "$bin" ]; then
    echo "SKIP $v k=$k: no $bin (run: ROI_K=$k bash build.sh $v)" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  # Resume: a leg that already produced both lines is done. Anything else
  # (empty, truncated, timed out) is re-run.
  if [ -f "$log" ] && grep -q '^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" && grep -q '\[roi\] MUL_MAT' "$log"; then
    echo "have $v k=$k"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "run  $v k=$k -> $log"
  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
      --mem-size 2000M --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms "$TIMEOUT" \
      "$bin" -- -m "$MODEL" -no-cnv $WARMUP --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 ) > "$log" 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  grep -E '\[roi\] MUL_MAT|^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" | sed "s/^/    $v k=$k: /"
  [ $rc -eq 0 ] || echo "    $v k=$k: exit $rc" >&2
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- reporting ---
# One log -> "cycles<TAB>nrows<TAB>tensor<TAB>shape", or a reason it is not a
# number. Kept in awk so the nrows gate and the cycle read come from the same
# pass over the same file.
read_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
  local log="$OUT/$1-k$2.log"
  [ -f "$log" ] || { printf 'MISSING\t\t\t\n'; return; }
  # [roi] MUL_MAT #51 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [2560 x 1024] nrows=4
  awk -v want="$WANT_NROWS" '
    /\[roi\] MUL_MAT/ {
      for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
        if ($i ~ /^src0=/)   { name = substr($i, 6) }
        if ($i ~ /^nrows=/)  { nrows = substr($i, 7) }
        if ($i ~ /^\[[0-9]+$/) { ne1 = $(i+2); sub(/\]$/, "", ne1)
                                 shape = substr($i, 2) "x" ne1 }
      }
    }
    /^\[andesim\] .* cycles/ { cyc = $2 }
    END {
      if (cyc == "")           { printf "PENDING\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
      if (nrows != want)       { printf "BAD-NROWS\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
      printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", cyc, nrows, name, shape
    }' "$log"
}

report() {
  printf '%s sweep -- %s, %s, nrows=%s\n\n' "$MODE" "$(basename "$MODEL")" "$ENGINE" "$WANT_NROWS"
  # Header is built from VARIANTS so a partial sweep still lines up.
  printf '%-4s %-16s %-12s' K tensor shape
  for v in $VARIANTS; do printf ' %14s' "$v"; done
  printf '\n'
  for k in $NODES; do
    local name="" shape="" cells=() f
    for v in $VARIANTS; do
      IFS=$'\t' read -r cyc nrows nm sh <<<"$(read_leg "$v" "$k")"
      [ -n "$nm" ] && name=$nm && shape=$sh
      cells+=("$cyc")
    done
    printf '%-4s %-16s %-12s' "$k" "${name%.weight}" "$shape"
    for f in "${cells[@]}"; do printf ' %14s' "$f"; done
    printf '\n'
  done
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- selfcheck ---
# The harness gate. Two legs with values published in opt_roadmap (F8 for the
# prefetch build, F9 for the vd4dot one), run AT THE SAME TIME. Passing means
# the invocation measures what it claims AND that two concurrent hybrid runs
# do not disturb each other -- which is what licenses the parallel sweep.
selfcheck() {
  [ "$MODE" = gemm ] || { echo "--selfcheck has reference values for MODE=gemm only" >&2; exit 2; }
  mkdir -p "$OUT"
  run_leg prefetch 51 & local p1=$!
  run_leg d4       51 & local p2=$!
  wait $p1 $p2
  local rc=0 got
  # opt_roadmap F8: prefill K=51 prefetch 1,651,949 (an earlier session read
  # 1,649,275 on the same build -- 0.16% apart, so allow 1%).
  # opt_roadmap F9: prefill K=51 d4 818,314.
  for pair in "prefetch:1651949" "d4:818314"; do
    got=$(read_leg "${pair%%:*}" 51 | cut -f1)
    local want=${pair##*:}
    if [[ "$got" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && awk -v g="$got" -v w="$want" 'BEGIN{exit !(g>w*0.99 && g<w*1.01)}'; then
      printf 'PASS %-8s k=51 %s cycles (published %s)\n' "${pair%%:*}" "$got" "$want"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %-8s k=51 got %s, published %s\n' "${pair%%:*}" "$got" "$want"
      rc=1
    fi
  done
  return $rc
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------- main ---
case "${1:-}" in
  --report)    report; exit 0 ;;
  --selfcheck) selfcheck; exit $? ;;
  --leg)       run_leg "$2" "$3"; exit $? ;;   # internal: one xargs slot
esac

[ -f "$MODEL" ] || { echo "no such model: $MODEL" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$OUT"
for k in $NODES; do for v in $VARIANTS; do echo "$v $k"; done; done \
  | xargs -P "$J" -n 2 bash "$0" --leg
echo
report

input.new_string:
# --------------------------------------------------------------- markdown ---
# The deliverable: profiling_data.md's table shape, generated from the logs so
# the document and the measurement can never drift apart. Reads the four
# stages BY NAME, so it does not care what order VARIANTS is in.
#   +repack    = upstream / baseline   (row-parallel 64x1 layout, F4)
#   +prefetch  = baseline / prefetch   (zicbop weight-stream prefetch, F7)
#   +vd4dots   = prefetch / d4         (nds.vd4dots.vv, F8+F9)
# A node missing any stage still prints its measured cells; only nodes with all
# four contribute to the geometric means, which is what "n =" reports.
md() {
  local k
  for k in $NODES; do
    local name shape cyc nrows nm sh v
    name=""; shape=""
    local -A c=()
    for v in pristine baseline prefetch d4; do
      IFS=$'\t' read -r cyc nrows nm sh <<<"$(read_leg "$v" "$k")"
      [ -n "$nm" ] && name=$nm && shape=$sh
      c[$v]=$cyc
    done
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
      "$k" "${name%.weight}" "$shape" \
      "${c[pristine]}" "${c[baseline]}" "${c[prefetch]}" "${c[d4]}"
  done | awk -F'\t' -v mode="$MODE" -v nr="$WANT_NROWS" -v eng="$ENGINE" '
    function num(x) { return (x ~ /^[0-9]+$/) }
    function fmt(x) { return num(x) ? sprintf("%'"'"'d", x+0) : x }
    function rat(a, b) { return (num(a) && num(b) && b+0 > 0) \
                                ? sprintf("%.2fx", a/b) : "-" }
    BEGIN {
      printf "| K | tensor | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |\n"
      printf "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n"
      n = 0
    }
    {
      split($3, d, "x"); w = d[1] * d[2]
      printf "| %s | `%s` | %s x %s | %'"'"'d | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n",
             $1, $2, d[1], d[2], w,
             fmt($4), fmt($5), fmt($6), fmt($7), rat($4, $7)
      # totals and geo means over the fully-measured nodes only
      if (num($4) && num($5) && num($6) && num($7)) {
        n++
        lr = log($4/$5); lp = log($5/$6); lv = log($6/$7)
        sr += lr; sp += lp; sv += lv
        if (n == 1 || lr < mnr) mnr = lr; if (n == 1 || lr > mxr) mxr = lr
        if (n == 1 || lp < mnp) mnp = lp; if (n == 1 || lp > mxp) mxp = lp
        if (n == 1 || lv < mnv) mnv = lv; if (n == 1 || lv > mxv) mxv = lv
        tu += $4; tb += $5; tp += $6; td += $7
      }
    }
    END {
      if (n) printf "| | **ALL %d** | | | **%'"'"'d** | **%'"'"'d** | **%'"'"'d** | **%'"'"'d** | **%.2fx** |\n",
                    n, tu, tb, tp, td, tu/td
      printf "\n### Where the %s speedup comes from (n = %d nodes with all four stages)\n\n", mode, n
      printf "| step | geo mean | min | max |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n"
      if (n) {
        printf "| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
               exp(sr/n), exp(mnr), exp(mxr)
        printf "| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
               exp(sp/n), exp(mnp), exp(mxp)
        printf "| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **%.2fx** | %.2fx | %.2fx |\n",
               exp(sv/n), exp(mnv), exp(mxv)
        printf "| **total** | **%.2fx** | | |\n", exp((sr+sp+sv)/n)
      }
      printf "\nengine %s, nrows=%d (%s path)\n", eng, nr, mode
    }'
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- selfcheck ---

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cycle sweep over the whole (build variant x MUL_MAT node) grid, in parallel.
#
# measure.sh runs ONE node across a few variants, serially, straight to the
# terminal. This runs the grid: every variant against every node, many legs at
# once, one log per leg, so a killed or timed-out leg is re-run on its own
# without repeating the rest. The deliverable is the table --report prints.
#
#   bash sweep.sh                      # gemm/prefill, K=50..56, all 4 variants
#   MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh            # the decode path instead
#   NODES="51 56" VARIANTS="prefetch d4" bash sweep.sh
#   J=4 bash sweep.sh                  # 4 legs at a time (default 8)
#   bash sweep.sh --report             # re-print the table, run nothing
#   bash sweep.sh --selfcheck          # gate: reproduce two published numbers
#
# MODE picks the ggml path by picking the prompt, which is the ONLY thing that
# decides it (opt_roadmap F7, "MEASUREMENT GOTCHA"):
#   gemv  the warmup forward pass          -> nrows=2, decode kernel
#   gemm  --no-warmup + a 4-token prompt   -> nrows=4, pure prefill, no gemv tail
# The [roi] line reports nrows, and a leg whose nrows disagrees with MODE is
# recorded as BAD-NROWS instead of as a number. This matters more than it
# looks: the wrong prompt measures the OTHER kernel and still prints a
# perfectly plausible cycle count, so the count alone can never catch it.
#
# Concurrency is safe: each hybrid run stages into its own make_temp_dir
# (andesim driver/manifest.cpp), and the cycle figure comes from a
# cycle-accurate RTL model, so host load cannot move it. --selfcheck proves
# both claims at once by running two legs together and comparing each against
# its published value.
#
# Slow: the RTL leg runs at a few kHz. A leg costs about 1 hour per 12M cycles,
# so the pristine ffn_* prefill legs are ~8 h each. Everything else is minutes.
set -u
export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
MODEL=${MODEL:-$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}
ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
MODE=${MODE:-gemm}
NODES=${NODES:-"50 51 52 53 54 55 56"}
VARIANTS=${VARIANTS:-"pristine baseline prefetch d4"}
J=${J:-8}
TIMEOUT=${TIMEOUT:-43200000}    # hybrid per-leg spawn timeout, ms (12 h)
OUT=${OUT:-$LLAMA/sweep-$MODE}

case "$MODE" in
  gemm) PROMPT="The capital of France"; WARMUP="--no-warmup"; WANT_NROWS=4 ;;
  gemv) PROMPT="The capital of France is"; WARMUP="";         WANT_NROWS=2 ;;
  *) echo "MODE must be gemm or gemv (got '$MODE')" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

bin_of() {  # $1 variant  $2 node -> the binary build.sh produced for that pair
  local suf=""; [ "$2" = 51 ] || suf="-k$2"
  printf '%s/bin-%s%s\n' "$LLAMA" "$1" "$suf"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- one leg ---
# Runs to completion, leaves everything in the log. Never parses; --report is
# the single parser, so a leg re-run and a fresh report cannot disagree.
run_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
  # Separate statements on purpose: bash expands every word of a `local` line
  # before it performs any of the assignments, so a log="...$v..." on the same
  # line would read an unset v.
  local v=$1 k=$2
  local log="$OUT/$v-k$k.log"
  local bin
  bin=$(bin_of "$v" "$k")
  if [ ! -x "$bin" ]; then
    echo "SKIP $v k=$k: no $bin (run: ROI_K=$k bash build.sh $v)" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  # Resume: a leg that already produced both lines is done. Anything else
  # (empty, truncated, timed out) is re-run.
  if [ -f "$log" ] && grep -q '^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" && grep -q '\[roi\] MUL_MAT' "$log"; then
    echo "have $v k=$k"
    return 0
  fi
  echo "run  $v k=$k -> $log"
  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
      --mem-size 2000M --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms "$TIMEOUT" \
      "$bin" -- -m "$MODEL" -no-cnv $WARMUP --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 ) > "$log" 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  grep -E '\[roi\] MUL_MAT|^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" | sed "s/^/    $v k=$k: /"
  [ $rc -eq 0 ] || echo "    $v k=$k: exit $rc" >&2
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- reporting ---
# One log -> "cycles<TAB>nrows<TAB>tensor<TAB>shape", or a reason it is not a
# number. Kept in awk so the nrows gate and the cycle read come from the same
# pass over the same file.
read_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
  local log="$OUT/$1-k$2.log"
  [ -f "$log" ] || { printf 'MISSING\t\t\t\n'; return; }
  # [roi] MUL_MAT #51 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [2560 x 1024] nrows=4
  awk -v want="$WANT_NROWS" '
    /\[roi\] MUL_MAT/ {
      for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
        if ($i ~ /^src0=/)   { name = substr($i, 6) }
        if ($i ~ /^nrows=/)  { nrows = substr($i, 7) }
        if ($i ~ /^\[[0-9]+$/) { ne1 = $(i+2); sub(/\]$/, "", ne1)
                                 shape = substr($i, 2) "x" ne1 }
      }
    }
    /^\[andesim\] .* cycles/ { cyc = $2 }
    END {
      if (cyc == "")           { printf "PENDING\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
      if (nrows != want)       { printf "BAD-NROWS\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", nrows, name, shape; exit }
      printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", cyc, nrows, name, shape
    }' "$log"
}

report() {
  printf '%s sweep -- %s, %s, nrows=%s\n\n' "$MODE" "$(basename "$MODEL")" "$ENGINE" "$WANT_NROWS"
  # Header is built from VARIANTS so a partial sweep still lines up.
  printf '%-4s %-16s %-12s' K tensor shape
  for v in $VARIANTS; do printf ' %14s' "$v"; done
  printf '\n'
  for k in $NODES; do
    local name="" shape="" cells=() f
    for v in $VARIANTS; do
      IFS=$'\t' read -r cyc nrows nm sh <<<"$(read_leg "$v" "$k")"
      [ -n "$nm" ] && name=$nm && shape=$sh
      cells+=("$cyc")
    done
    printf '%-4s %-16s %-12s' "$k" "${name%.weight}" "$shape"
    for f in "${cells[@]}"; do printf ' %14s' "$f"; done
    printf '\n'
  done
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- selfcheck ---
# The harness gate. Two legs with values published in opt_roadmap (F8 for the
# prefetch build, F9 for the vd4dot one), run AT THE SAME TIME. Passing means
# the invocation measures what it claims AND that two concurrent hybrid runs
# do not disturb each other -- which is what licenses the parallel sweep.
selfcheck() {
  [ "$MODE" = gemm ] || { echo "--selfcheck has reference values for MODE=gemm only" >&2; exit 2; }
  mkdir -p "$OUT"
  run_leg prefetch 51 & local p1=$!
  run_leg d4       51 & local p2=$!
  wait $p1 $p2
  local rc=0 got
  # opt_roadmap F8: prefill K=51 prefetch 1,651,949 (an earlier session read
  # 1,649,275 on the same build -- 0.16% apart, so allow 1%).
  # opt_roadmap F9: prefill K=51 d4 818,314.
  for pair in "prefetch:1651949" "d4:818314"; do
    got=$(read_leg "${pair%%:*}" 51 | cut -f1)
    local want=${pair##*:}
    if [[ "$got" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && awk -v g="$got" -v w="$want" 'BEGIN{exit !(g>w*0.99 && g<w*1.01)}'; then
      printf 'PASS %-8s k=51 %s cycles (published %s)\n' "${pair%%:*}" "$got" "$want"
    else
      printf 'FAIL %-8s k=51 got %s, published %s\n' "${pair%%:*}" "$got" "$want"
      rc=1
    fi
  done
  return $rc
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------- main ---
case "${1:-}" in
  --report)    report; exit 0 ;;
  --selfcheck) selfcheck; exit $? ;;
  --leg)       run_leg "$2" "$3"; exit $? ;;   # internal: one xargs slot
esac

[ -f "$MODEL" ] || { echo "no such model: $MODEL" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$OUT"
for k in $NODES; do for v in $VARIANTS; do echo "$v $k"; done; done \
  | xargs -P "$J" -n 2 bash "$0" --leg
echo
report

content.text:
Status so far:

**Harness built and gated.** `sweep.sh` runs the whole (variant x node) grid in parallel, one log per leg, resumable. Its `--selfcheck` reproduced two published numbers while running both legs concurrently:

| leg | measured | published (opt_roadmap) | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| K=51 prefetch, prefill | 1,651,086 | 1,651,949 | 0.05% |
| K=51 d4, prefill | 823,397 | 818,314 | 0.62% |

That proves the invocation measures the gemm path *and* that concurrent andesim runs don't disturb each other - which is what licenses running 22 legs at once.

**Two sweeps now in flight** on the existing 28 binaries (no rebuilds needed):
- gemm/prefill, K=50..56 x 4 variants, `nrows=4`
- gemv/decode, same grid, `nrows=2` - needed because the existing decode data has no `baseline` (repack-only) column except at K=51, and its `d4` numbers are pre-F9, so it cannot be compared against F9-era gemm numbers.

Two harness bugs found and fixed before they cost sim time: a `local v=$1 log="...$v..."` that read an unset `v` (bash expands all words before assigning any), and - more dangerous - an unrecognized flag falling through to *start the whole sweep*; unknown flags now exit 2.

One finding already grounded in code rather than assumed: `ggml-cpu.c:257` sets Q1_0 `.nrows = 1`, and `mul_mat_one_chunk` issues one `vec_dot` per (weight row, token). Upstream is therefore exactly linear in token count - 2,238,337 cycles/token at decode vs 2,218,812 at prefill on K=51. So any extra prefill speedup comes from the repack **gemm kernel's M-tile amortization**, not from upstream being weaker at prefill.

Mechanism confirmed in source. Per 4 columns:

| kernel | vlm mask loads | vmerge | `nds.vd4dots.vv` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv (`q1_vd4dots_x4_m2`, :1809) | 4 | 4 | 4 |

content.text:
The first complete gemm node, all four stages measured fresh in one session. Set against the published decode chain for the same tensor:

| stage | gemm (prefill, 4 tok) | gemv (decode, 2 tok) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream | 8,879,897 | 4,476,168 |
| +repack | 1,695,440 (**5.24x**) | 2,144,213 (**2.09x**) |
| +prefetch | 1,651,086 (**1.03x**) | 1,389,236 (**1.54x**) |
| +vd4dots | 823,397 (**2.01x**) | 362,799 (**3.83x**) |
| **total** | **10.78x** | **12.34x** |

The totals are close, but the composition is inverted: prefill takes almost its whole win from the **repack layout** (5.24x), while decode spreads it across prefetch and vd4dots. That is exactly what the kernel structure predicts - the gemm fires 4 dots per weight load, so the layout change buys 4x amortization up front, leaving far less memory stall for prefetch to hide and less instruction pressure for vd4dots to remove.

Waiting on the remaining 5 nodes to see whether this holds shape-independently.

# Bonsai-4B prefill profiling: measured cycles per MUL_MAT node (gemm path)

The prefill counterpart of `profiling_data.md`. Same four build stages, same
engine, same per-node marker ROI -- but on the **gemm** path (`nrows=4`)
instead of the decode gemv path.

Generated 2026-08-28. Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one
MUL_MAT node, produced by `bash sweep.sh` and re-readable with
`bash sweep.sh --md`.

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 |
| Model | `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`, qwen3, 36 layers, 572 MB |
| Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--mem-size 2000M -t 1` |
| Path | prefill / gemm, `nrows=4` (asserted per leg from the `[roi]` line) |
| Node id | `ROI_K` = index of the MUL_MAT in graph order, 1-based |
| Nodes | layer 7, K=50..56 -- all 7 distinct Q1_0 shapes in the model |

The path is selected by the prompt, and by nothing else:

| path | invocation | `nrows` |
|---|---|---:|
| gemv / decode | warmup forward pass | 2 |
| gemm / prefill | `--no-warmup` + a 4-token prompt | 4 |

A 5-token prompt would give gemm(4) + a gemv(1) tail and silently mix the two
kernels, so every leg re-reads `nrows` from its own `[roi]` line and refuses to
report a number that disagrees with the requested path.

## Build variants

| name | flags | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` | upstream llama.cpp |
| `baseline` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` | + row-parallel 64x1 repack |
| `prefetch` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` | + zicbop prefetch = **standard RVV** |
| `d4` | + `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON`, `Q1_VD4DOT=1` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |

## Layer 7, prefill (`nrows=4`)

<!-- BEGIN GEMM TABLE (regenerate: bash sweep.sh --md) -->
| K | tensor | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | `blk.7.attn_q` | 2560 x 4096 | 10,485,760 | 35,510,678 | 5,566,590 | 5,386,377 | 2,071,451 | 17.14x |
| 51 | `blk.7.attn_v` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 8,879,897 | 1,695,440 | 1,651,086 | 823,397 | 10.78x |
| 52 | `blk.7.attn_k` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 8,929,195 | 1,696,273 | 1,651,132 | 823,291 | 10.85x |
| 53 | `blk.7.attn_output` | 4096 x 2560 | 10,485,760 | PENDING | 5,844,812 | 5,592,124 | 2,357,551 | - |
| 54 | `blk.7.ffn_gate` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 12,701,128 | 12,066,600 | 3,972,668 | - |
| 55 | `blk.7.ffn_up` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 12,696,438 | 12,069,169 | 3,971,366 | - |
| 56 | `blk.7.ffn_down` | 9728 x 2560 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 14,196,333 | 13,483,443 | 5,709,937 | - |
| | **ALL 3** | | | **53,319,770** | **8,958,303** | **8,688,595** | **3,718,139** | **14.34x** |

### Where the gemm speedup comes from (n = 3 nodes with all four stages)

| step | geo mean | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **5.60x** | 5.24x | 6.38x |
| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **1.03x** | 1.03x | 1.03x |
| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **2.19x** | 2.01x | 2.60x |
| **total** | **12.61x** | | |
<!-- END GEMM TABLE -->

The four `upstream` cells still running are the most expensive legs in the
grid: at roughly 1 cycle per weight per token, `pristine` ffn_down is ~97M
cycles, about 8 hours of RTL. The three completed nodes already fix the shape
of the answer; the remaining four extend it, they do not change it.

## The finding: prefill and decode reach the same place by different routes

Per-stage, the same tensor (`blk.7.attn_v`), prefill measured here and decode
from the matching sweep:

| stage | gemm (prefill, 4 tok) | gemv (decode, 2 tok) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream | 8,879,897 | 4,478,183 |
| +repack | 1,695,440 (**5.24x**) | 2,145,948 (**2.09x**) |
| +prefetch | 1,651,086 (**1.03x**) | 1,387,101 (**1.55x**) |
| +vd4dots | 823,397 (**2.01x**) | -- (published 3.83x) |

The totals land close together, but almost none of it is the same work:

- **Prefill takes its win from the layout.** 5.24-6.38x at the repack stage,
  against 2.09x for decode.
- **Prefetch is nearly a no-op for prefill** (1.03x) where it is worth 1.55x
  for decode.
- **vd4dots pays about half as much** for prefill (2.01-2.60x vs 3.83x).

### Why -- both halves are visible in the source

**Upstream has no prefill kernel at all.** `GGML_TYPE_Q1_0` sets `.nrows = 1`
(`ggml-cpu.c:257`), and `ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat_one_chunk` issues one
`vec_dot` per (weight row, token) pair. So upstream cost is exactly linear in
token count, which the measurement confirms on two independent nodes:

| node | 2 tokens | 4 tokens | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| K=51 `attn_v` | 4,478,183 | 8,879,897 | 1.98x |
| K=52 `attn_k` | 4,513,768 | 8,929,195 | 1.98x |

**The repack gemm kernel amortizes every weight-side operation across the
M-tile.** Per 4 columns of weights:

| kernel | vlm mask loads | vmerge | `nds.vd4dots.vv` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv (`q1_vd4dots_x4_m2`, `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1809`) | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| gemm (`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`) | 1 | 1 | 4 |

The gemm loads one weight vector and fires four dots against it, one per token
(`q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2` reuses `%[w]` across accumulators `a0..a3`). That single
change is worth ~4x on all weight traffic, which is why the layout stage pays
so much more at prefill -- and, having removed the memory stall up front, why
there is little left for the prefetch stage to hide.

## Notes

- **Identical shapes give identical cycles.** `attn_v` and `attn_k` are both
  2560x1024 and agree to 0.003% at `prefetch` and 0.01% at `d4`; `ffn_gate` and
  `ffn_up` are both 2560x9728 and agree to 0.02%. That is the noise floor.
- **Total speedup grows with row count.** attn_q (4096 rows) reaches 17.14x
  where attn_v (1024 rows) reaches 10.78x. Upstream scales exactly 4x between
  them (8.88M -> 35.5M) but the vd4dot kernel scales only 2.52x
  (823K -> 2.07M), because per-call fixed costs -- notably the once-per-call
  activation restaging -- amortize over more 64-row tiles.
- **The prefetch stage tracks L3 residency.** 1.027x on attn_v (360 KB
  repacked, fits the 2 MB L3) against 1.053x on ffn_down (3.5 MB, does not).
  Weight reuse across the M-tile already hides the rest.
- **Cross-checks against earlier sessions.** This grid re-derived five numbers
  recorded by previous sessions, all within 1%: gemm K=51 `baseline`
  (1,695,440 vs 1,696,704), `prefetch` (1,651,086 vs 1,651,949), `d4` (823,397
  vs 818,314), gemm K=56 `prefetch` (13,483,443 vs 13,474,132) and `d4`
  (5,709,937 vs 5,683,029).

## Reproducing

```sh
bash sweep.sh --selfcheck    # gate: re-derive two published K=51 numbers
bash sweep.sh                # the prefill grid, K=50..56 x 4 variants
MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh      # the matching decode grid
bash sweep.sh --md           # regenerate the table above from the logs
```

Legs are independent, resumable, and safe to run concurrently: each hybrid run
stages into its own temp dir, and the cycle figure comes from a cycle-accurate
RTL model, so host load cannot move it.

# Bonsai-4B prefill profiling: measured cycles per MUL_MAT node (gemm path)

The prefill counterpart of `profiling_data.md`. Same four build stages, same
engine, same per-node marker ROI -- on the **gemm** path (`nrows=4`) instead of
the decode gemv path, plus a matching gemv sweep so the two are comparable
node for node.

Generated 2026-08-28. Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one
MUL_MAT node, produced by `bash sweep.sh` and regenerable with
`bash sweep.sh --md`.

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 |
| Model | `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`, qwen3, 36 layers, 572 MB |
| Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--mem-size 2000M -t 1` |
| Node id | `ROI_K` = index of the MUL_MAT in graph order, 1-based |
| Nodes | layer 7, K=50..56 -- all 7 distinct Q1_0 shapes in the model |

The path is selected by the prompt, and by nothing else:

| path | invocation | `nrows` |
|---|---|---:|
| gemv / decode | warmup forward pass | 2 |
| gemm / prefill | `--no-warmup` + a 4-token prompt | 4 |

A 5-token prompt would give gemm(4) plus a gemv(1) tail and silently mix the
two kernels, so every leg re-reads `nrows` from its own `[roi]` line and
refuses to report a number that disagrees with the requested path.

## Build variants

| name | flags | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` | upstream llama.cpp |
| `baseline` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` | + row-parallel 64x1 repack |
| `prefetch` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` | + zicbop prefetch = **standard RVV** |
| `d4` | + `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON`, `Q1_VD4DOT=1` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |

## Layer 7, prefill / gemm (`nrows=4`)

<!-- BEGIN GEMM TABLE (regenerate: bash sweep.sh --md) -->
| K | tensor | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | `blk.7.attn_q` | 2560 x 4096 | 10,485,760 | 35,510,678 | 5,566,590 | 5,386,377 | 2,071,451 | 17.14x |
| 51 | `blk.7.attn_v` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 8,879,897 | 1,695,440 | 1,651,086 | 823,397 | 10.78x |
| 52 | `blk.7.attn_k` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 8,929,195 | 1,696,273 | 1,651,132 | 823,291 | 10.85x |
| 53 | `blk.7.attn_output` | 4096 x 2560 | 10,485,760 | 36,923,068 | 5,844,812 | 5,592,124 | 2,357,551 | 15.66x |
| 54 | `blk.7.ffn_gate` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | 82,747,014 | 12,701,128 | 12,066,600 | 3,972,668 | 20.83x |
| 55 | `blk.7.ffn_up` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 12,696,438 | 12,069,169 | 3,971,366 | - |
| 56 | `blk.7.ffn_down` | 9728 x 2560 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 14,196,333 | 13,483,443 | 5,709,937 | - |
| | **ALL 5** | | | **172,989,852** | **27,504,243** | **26,347,319** | **10,048,358** | **17.22x** |

### Where the gemm speedup comes from (n = 5 nodes with all four stages)

| step | geo mean | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **5.91x** | 5.24x | 6.51x |
| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **1.04x** | 1.03x | 1.05x |
| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **2.37x** | 2.01x | 3.04x |
| **total** | **14.56x** | | |
<!-- END GEMM TABLE -->

The two `upstream` cells still running are the most expensive legs in the grid
(`pristine` ffn_up and ffn_down, ~83M and ~97M cycles).

## Layer 7, decode / gemv (`nrows=2`), measured the same way

<!-- BEGIN GEMV TABLE (regenerate: MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh --md) -->
| K | tensor | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | `blk.7.attn_q` | 2560 x 4096 | 10,485,760 | 17,981,071 | 8,516,129 | 5,475,562 | 1,437,326 | 12.51x |
| 51 | `blk.7.attn_v` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 4,478,183 | 2,145,948 | 1,387,101 | 381,355 | 11.74x |
| 52 | `blk.7.attn_k` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 4,513,768 | 2,148,809 | 1,388,277 | 381,654 | 11.83x |
| 53 | `blk.7.attn_output` | 4096 x 2560 | 10,485,760 | 18,320,199 | 8,583,053 | 5,490,245 | 1,520,976 | 12.05x |
| 54 | `blk.7.ffn_gate` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | 42,194,328 | 20,243,782 | 12,958,214 | 3,326,210 | 12.69x |
| 55 | `blk.7.ffn_up` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | 42,151,859 | 20,244,994 | 12,960,767 | 3,326,247 | 12.67x |
| 56 | `blk.7.ffn_down` | 9728 x 2560 | 24,903,680 | 49,058,107 | 20,844,150 | 12,991,435 | 3,770,805 | 13.01x |
| | **ALL 7** | | | **178,697,515** | **82,726,865** | **52,651,601** | **14,144,573** | **12.63x** |

### Where the gemv speedup comes from (n = 7 nodes with all four stages)

| step | geo mean | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **2.13x** | 2.08x | 2.35x |
| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **1.56x** | 1.55x | 1.60x |
| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **3.70x** | 3.45x | 3.90x |
| **total** | **12.35x** | | |
<!-- END GEMV TABLE -->

## The finding: same destination, opposite routes

| step | gemm (prefill) | gemv (decode) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream to +repack | **5.91x** | 2.13x |
| +repack to +prefetch | **1.04x** | 1.56x |
| +prefetch to +vd4dots | **2.37x** | 3.70x |
| **total** | **14.56x** | **12.35x** |

Per node, so the spread is visible:

| K | tensor | repack gemm | repack gemv | prefetch gemm | prefetch gemv | vd4dots gemm | vd4dots gemv | total gemm | total gemv |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | `blk.7.attn_q` | 6.38x | 2.11x | 1.03x | 1.56x | 2.60x | 3.81x | **17.14x** | **12.51x** |
| 51 | `blk.7.attn_v` | 5.24x | 2.09x | 1.03x | 1.55x | 2.01x | 3.64x | **10.78x** | **11.74x** |
| 52 | `blk.7.attn_k` | 5.26x | 2.10x | 1.03x | 1.55x | 2.01x | 3.64x | **10.85x** | **11.83x** |
| 53 | `blk.7.attn_output` | 6.32x | 2.13x | 1.05x | 1.56x | 2.37x | 3.61x | **15.66x** | **12.05x** |
| 54 | `blk.7.ffn_gate` | 6.51x | 2.08x | 1.05x | 1.56x | 3.04x | 3.90x | **20.83x** | **12.69x** |
| 55 | `blk.7.ffn_up` | - | 2.08x | 1.05x | 1.56x | 3.04x | 3.90x | - | **12.67x** |
| 56 | `blk.7.ffn_down` | - | 2.35x | 1.05x | 1.60x | 2.36x | 3.45x | - | **13.01x** |

Two things stand out.

1. **Prefill buys its win from the layout, decode from the instructions.**
   Repack is worth 5.9x to prefill and 2.1x to decode; prefetch and vd4dots are
   each worth roughly half as much to prefill as to decode.
2. **Decode's speedup is shape-invariant, prefill's is not.** gemv spans
   11.74x-13.01x across a 9.5x range of node sizes (a 1.11x spread). gemm spans
   10.78x-20.83x (1.93x). On the smallest node prefill gains *less* than decode;
   on the largest it gains far more.

### Why prefill wins at the layout stage

**Upstream has no prefill kernel at all.** `GGML_TYPE_Q1_0` sets `.nrows = 1`
(`ggml-cpu.c:257`), and `ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat_one_chunk` issues one
`vec_dot` per (weight row, token) pair, so upstream cost is exactly linear in
token count. Measured on three independent nodes:

| node | 2 tokens | 4 tokens | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| K=51 `attn_v` | 4,478,183 | 8,879,897 | 1.98x |
| K=52 `attn_k` | 4,513,768 | 8,929,195 | 1.98x |
| K=53 `attn_output` | 18,320,199 | 36,923,068 | 2.02x |

**The repack gemm amortizes every weight-side operation across the M-tile.**
Per 4 columns of weights:

| kernel | vlm mask loads | vmerge | `nds.vd4dots.vv` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv (`q1_vd4dots_x4_m2`, `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1809`) | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| gemm (`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`) | 1 | 1 | 4 |

The gemm loads one weight vector and fires four dots against it, one per token
(`q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2` reuses `%[w]` across accumulators `a0..a3`). That is ~4x
off all weight traffic in one step -- and, having removed the memory stall up
front, it is also why the prefetch stage has almost nothing left to hide.

### Why prefill loses on small tensors: a scalar activation quantizer

attn_q, attn_v, attn_k, ffn_gate and ffn_up all have `ne0 = 2560` and differ
only in row count, so a node's cost splits into a per-call constant and a
per-64-row-tile term. Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles`:

| | fixed per call `F` | per tile `T` | per tile **per token** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv `d4` (2 tok) | 39,491 | 21,638 | 10,819 |
| gemm `d4` (4 tok) | 489,581 | 23,036 | **5,759** |

The fit is tight (gemv residuals within 1.1%). In steady state the gemm is
**1.88x more efficient per token**, exactly as the M-tile sharing predicts. But
it carries **12.4x the per-call fixed cost**, and that constant is what decides
the small nodes: `F` is 59% of attn_v's 823,397 total and only 12% of
ffn_gate's 3,972,668.

`F` is not part of the kernel. Fitting the same model to each repack variant:

| variant | fixed `F` | per tile `T` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `baseline` | 398,003 | 80,915 |
| `prefetch` | 441,355 | 76,544 |
| `d4` | 489,581 | 23,036 |

`T` collapses 3.5x as the kernel improves; `F` does not move. It is the shared
activation path, and the source says what it is. `forward_mul_mat` quantizes
activations before the kernel runs (`repack.cpp:4456-4469`), and the routine it
picks depends on the token count:

- **4 tokens** (`ne11 - ne11 % 4 == 4`) take
  `ggml_quantize_mat_t<1, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0>`, which selects
  `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` -- a **pure scalar** loop
  (`repack.cpp:51`, its own comment says `// scalar`): per 32-column block, 128
  `fabsf` for the amax scan plus 128 `roundf` plus the de-interleave index
  arithmetic. Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the
  measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`.
- **2 tokens** are not a multiple of 4, so they fall through to `from_float` =
  `quantize_row_q8_0`, which **is** RVV-vectorized on RISC-V
  (`arch/riscv/quants.c:32`, gated only on `__riscv_v`).

So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one. That is the
whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap, and at ~490K cycles per node it is now the largest

# Bonsai-4B prefill profiling: measured cycles per MUL_MAT node (gemm path)

The prefill counterpart of `profiling_data.md`. Same four build stages, same
engine, same per-node marker ROI -- on the **gemm** path (`nrows=4`) instead of
the decode gemv path, plus a matching gemv sweep so the two are comparable
node for node.

Generated 2026-08-28. Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one
MUL_MAT node, produced by `bash sweep.sh` and regenerable with
`bash sweep.sh --md`.

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 |
| Model | `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`, qwen3, 36 layers, 572 MB |
| Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--mem-size 2000M -t 1` |
| Node id | `ROI_K` = index of the MUL_MAT in graph order, 1-based |
| Nodes | layer 7, K=50..56 -- all 7 distinct Q1_0 shapes in the model |

The path is selected by the prompt, and by nothing else:

| path | invocation | `nrows` |
|---|---|---:|
| gemv / decode | warmup forward pass | 2 |
| gemm / prefill | `--no-warmup` + a 4-token prompt | 4 |

A 5-token prompt would give gemm(4) plus a gemv(1) tail and silently mix the
two kernels, so every leg re-reads `nrows` from its own `[roi]` line and
refuses to report a number that disagrees with the requested path.

## Build variants

| name | flags | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` | upstream llama.cpp |
| `baseline` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` | + row-parallel 64x1 repack |
| `prefetch` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` | + zicbop prefetch = **standard RVV** |
| `d4` | + `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON`, `Q1_VD4DOT=1` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |

## Layer 7, prefill / gemm (`nrows=4`)

<!-- BEGIN GEMM TABLE (regenerate: bash sweep.sh --md) -->
| K | tensor | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | `blk.7.attn_q` | 2560 x 4096 | 10,485,760 | 35,510,678 | 5,566,590 | 5,386,377 | 2,071,451 | 17.14x |
| 51 | `blk.7.attn_v` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 8,879,897 | 1,695,440 | 1,651,086 | 823,397 | 10.78x |
| 52 | `blk.7.attn_k` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 8,929,195 | 1,696,273 | 1,651,132 | 823,291 | 10.85x |
| 53 | `blk.7.attn_output` | 4096 x 2560 | 10,485,760 | 36,923,068 | 5,844,812 | 5,592,124 | 2,357,551 | 15.66x |
| 54 | `blk.7.ffn_gate` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | 82,747,014 | 12,701,128 | 12,066,600 | 3,972,668 | 20.83x |
| 55 | `blk.7.ffn_up` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 12,696,438 | 12,069,169 | 3,971,366 | - |
| 56 | `blk.7.ffn_down` | 9728 x 2560 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 14,196,333 | 13,483,443 | 5,709,937 | - |
| | **ALL 5** | | | **172,989,852** | **27,504,243** | **26,347,319** | **10,048,358** | **17.22x** |

### Where the gemm speedup comes from (n = 5 nodes with all four stages)

| step | geo mean | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **5.91x** | 5.24x | 6.51x |
| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **1.04x** | 1.03x | 1.05x |
| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **2.37x** | 2.01x | 3.04x |
| **total** | **14.56x** | | |
<!-- END GEMM TABLE -->

The two `upstream` cells still running are the most expensive legs in the grid
(`pristine` ffn_up and ffn_down, ~83M and ~97M cycles).

## Layer 7, decode / gemv (`nrows=2`), measured the same way

<!-- BEGIN GEMV TABLE (regenerate: MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh --md) -->
| K | tensor | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | `blk.7.attn_q` | 2560 x 4096 | 10,485,760 | 17,981,071 | 8,516,129 | 5,475,562 | 1,437,326 | 12.51x |
| 51 | `blk.7.attn_v` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 4,478,183 | 2,145,948 | 1,387,101 | 381,355 | 11.74x |
| 52 | `blk.7.attn_k` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 4,513,768 | 2,148,809 | 1,388,277 | 381,654 | 11.83x |
| 53 | `blk.7.attn_output` | 4096 x 2560 | 10,485,760 | 18,320,199 | 8,583,053 | 5,490,245 | 1,520,976 | 12.05x |
| 54 | `blk.7.ffn_gate` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | 42,194,328 | 20,243,782 | 12,958,214 | 3,326,210 | 12.69x |
| 55 | `blk.7.ffn_up` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | 42,151,859 | 20,244,994 | 12,960,767 | 3,326,247 | 12.67x |
| 56 | `blk.7.ffn_down` | 9728 x 2560 | 24,903,680 | 49,058,107 | 20,844,150 | 12,991,435 | 3,770,805 | 13.01x |
| | **ALL 7** | | | **178,697,515** | **82,726,865** | **52,651,601** | **14,144,573** | **12.63x** |

### Where the gemv speedup comes from (n = 7 nodes with all four stages)

| step | geo mean | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **2.13x** | 2.08x | 2.35x |
| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **1.56x** | 1.55x | 1.60x |
| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **3.70x** | 3.45x | 3.90x |
| **total** | **12.35x** | | |
<!-- END GEMV TABLE -->

## The finding: same destination, opposite routes

| step | gemm (prefill) | gemv (decode) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream to +repack | **5.91x** | 2.13x |
| +repack to +prefetch | **1.04x** | 1.56x |
| +prefetch to +vd4dots | **2.37x** | 3.70x |
| **total** | **14.56x** | **12.35x** |

Per node, so the spread is visible:

| K | tensor | repack gemm | repack gemv | prefetch gemm | prefetch gemv | vd4dots gemm | vd4dots gemv | total gemm | total gemv |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | `blk.7.attn_q` | 6.38x | 2.11x | 1.03x | 1.56x | 2.60x | 3.81x | **17.14x** | **12.51x** |
| 51 | `blk.7.attn_v` | 5.24x | 2.09x | 1.03x | 1.55x | 2.01x | 3.64x | **10.78x** | **11.74x** |
| 52 | `blk.7.attn_k` | 5.26x | 2.10x | 1.03x | 1.55x | 2.01x | 3.64x | **10.85x** | **11.83x** |
| 53 | `blk.7.attn_output` | 6.32x | 2.13x | 1.05x | 1.56x | 2.37x | 3.61x | **15.66x** | **12.05x** |
| 54 | `blk.7.ffn_gate` | 6.51x | 2.08x | 1.05x | 1.56x | 3.04x | 3.90x | **20.83x** | **12.69x** |
| 55 | `blk.7.ffn_up` | - | 2.08x | 1.05x | 1.56x | 3.04x | 3.90x | - | **12.67x** |
| 56 | `blk.7.ffn_down` | - | 2.35x | 1.05x | 1.60x | 2.36x | 3.45x | - | **13.01x** |

Two things stand out.

1. **Prefill buys its win from the layout, decode from the instructions.**
   Repack is worth 5.9x to prefill and 2.1x to decode; prefetch and vd4dots are
   each worth roughly half as much to prefill as to decode.
2. **Decode's speedup is shape-invariant, prefill's is not.** gemv spans
   11.74x-13.01x across a 9.5x range of node sizes (a 1.11x spread). gemm spans
   10.78x-20.83x (1.93x). On the smallest node prefill gains *less* than decode;
   on the largest it gains far more.

### Why prefill wins at the layout stage

**Upstream has no prefill kernel at all.** `GGML_TYPE_Q1_0` sets `.nrows = 1`
(`ggml-cpu.c:257`), and `ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat_one_chunk` issues one
`vec_dot` per (weight row, token) pair, so upstream cost is exactly linear in
token count. Measured on three independent nodes:

| node | 2 tokens | 4 tokens | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| K=51 `attn_v` | 4,478,183 | 8,879,897 | 1.98x |
| K=52 `attn_k` | 4,513,768 | 8,929,195 | 1.98x |
| K=53 `attn_output` | 18,320,199 | 36,923,068 | 2.02x |

**The repack gemm amortizes every weight-side operation across the M-tile.**
Per 4 columns of weights:

| kernel | vlm mask loads | vmerge | `nds.vd4dots.vv` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv (`q1_vd4dots_x4_m2`, `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1809`) | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| gemm (`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`) | 1 | 1 | 4 |

The gemm loads one weight vector and fires four dots against it, one per token
(`q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2` reuses `%[w]` across accumulators `a0..a3`). That is ~4x
off all weight traffic in one step -- and, having removed the memory stall up
front, it is also why the prefetch stage has almost nothing left to hide.

### Why prefill loses on small tensors: a scalar activation quantizer

attn_q, attn_v, attn_k, ffn_gate and ffn_up all have `ne0 = 2560` and differ
only in row count, so a node's cost splits into a per-call constant and a
per-64-row-tile term. Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles`:

| | fixed per call `F` | per tile `T` | per tile **per token** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv `d4` (2 tok) | 39,491 | 21,638 | 10,819 |
| gemm `d4` (4 tok) | 489,581 | 23,036 | **5,759** |

The fit is tight (gemv residuals within 1.1%). In steady state the gemm is
**1.88x more efficient per token**, exactly as the M-tile sharing predicts. But
it carries **12.4x the per-call fixed cost**, and that constant is what decides
the small nodes: `F` is 59% of attn_v's 823,397 total and only 12% of
ffn_gate's 3,972,668.

`F` is not part of the kernel. Fitting the same model to each repack variant:

| variant | fixed `F` | per tile `T` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `baseline` | 398,003 | 80,915 |
| `prefetch` | 441,355 | 76,544 |
| `d4` | 489,581 | 23,036 |

`T` collapses 3.5x as the kernel improves; `F` does not move. It is the shared
activation path, and the source says what it is. `forward_mul_mat` quantizes
activations before the kernel runs (`repack.cpp:4456-4469`), and the routine it
picks depends on the token count:

- **4 tokens** (`ne11 - ne11 % 4 == 4`) take
  `ggml_quantize_mat_t<1, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0>`, which selects
  `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` -- a **pure scalar** loop
  (`repack.cpp:51`, its own comment says `// scalar`): per 32-column block, 128
  `fabsf` for the amax scan plus 128 `roundf` plus the de-interleave index
  arithmetic. Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the
  measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`.
- **2 tokens** are not a multiple of 4, so they fall through to `from_float` =
  `quantize_row_q8_0`, which **is** RVV-vectorized on RISC-V
  (`arch/riscv/quants.c:32`, gated only on `__riscv_v`).

So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one. That is the
whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap, and at ~490K cycles per node it is now the largest
single item in a small prefill matmul -- bigger than the kernel it feeds.

## Notes

- **Identical shapes give identical cycles.** attn_v and attn_k (both
  2560x1024) agree to 0.003% at `prefetch` and 0.01% at `d4`; ffn_gate and
  ffn_up (both 2560x9728) agree to 0.02%. That is the noise floor.
- **The prefetch stage tracks L3 residency.** 1.03x on attn_v (360 KB repacked,
  fits the 2 MB L3) against 1.05x on ffn_down (3.5 MB, does not). Weight reuse
  across the M-tile already hides the rest.
- **Cross-checks against earlier sessions**, all within 1%: gemm K=51
  `baseline` (1,695,440 vs 1,696,704), `prefetch` (1,651,086 vs 1,651,949),
  `d4` (823,397 vs 818,314); gemm K=56 `prefetch` (13,483,443 vs 13,474,132);
  gemv K=51 `pristine` (4,478,183 vs 4,476,168), `baseline` (2,145,948 vs
  2,144,213), `prefetch` (1,387,101 vs 1,389,236); gemv K=56 `pristine`
  (49,058,107 vs 49,054,708). The gemv layer-7 aggregate prefetch-vs-pristine
  ratio, 178,697,515 / 52,651,601 = 3.394x, reproduces the 3.39x that two
  earlier sessions measured independently.
- **One cross-check is not within 1%:** gemv `d4` K=51 measures 381,355 here
  against a published 362,799 (5.1%). The published figure dates from
  2026-08-01 and these binaries from 2026-08-19. Every number in this document
  comes from that one binary set, so the tables are internally consistent; the
  older value is simply not from the same build.

## Reproducing

```sh

bash sweep.sh                # the prefill grid, K=50..56 x 4 variants
MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh      # the matching decode grid
bash sweep.sh --md           # regenerate the tables above from the logs
```
