# Bonsai-4B prefill profiling: measured cycles per MUL_MAT node (gemm path)

The prefill counterpart of `profiling_data.md`. Same four build stages, same
engine, same per-node marker ROI -- but on the **gemm** path (`nrows=4`)
instead of the decode gemv path.

Generated 2026-08-28. Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one
MUL_MAT node, produced by `bash sweep.sh` and re-readable with
`bash sweep.sh --md`.

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 |
| Model | `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`, qwen3, 36 layers, 572 MB |
| Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--mem-size 2000M -t 1` |
| Path | prefill / gemm, `nrows=4` (asserted per leg from the `[roi]` line) |
| Node id | `ROI_K` = index of the MUL_MAT in graph order, 1-based |
| Nodes | layer 7, K=50..56 -- all 7 distinct Q1_0 shapes in the model |

The path is selected by the prompt, and by nothing else:

| path | invocation | `nrows` |
|---|---|---:|
| gemv / decode | warmup forward pass | 2 |
| gemm / prefill | `--no-warmup` + a 4-token prompt | 4 |

A 5-token prompt would give gemm(4) + a gemv(1) tail and silently mix the two
kernels, so every leg re-reads `nrows` from its own `[roi]` line and refuses to
report a number that disagrees with the requested path.

## Build variants

| name | flags | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` | upstream llama.cpp |
| `baseline` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=0` | + row-parallel 64x1 repack |
| `prefetch` | repack ON, `Q1_PREFETCH_DIST=1` | + zicbop prefetch = **standard RVV** |
| `d4` | + `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON`, `Q1_VD4DOT=1` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |

## Layer 7, prefill (`nrows=4`)

<!-- BEGIN GEMM TABLE (regenerate: bash sweep.sh --md) -->
| K | tensor | ne0 x ne1 | weights | upstream | +repack | +prefetch | +vd4dots | total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 50 | `blk.7.attn_q` | 2560 x 4096 | 10,485,760 | 35,510,678 | 5,566,590 | 5,386,377 | 2,071,451 | 17.14x |
| 51 | `blk.7.attn_v` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 8,879,897 | 1,695,440 | 1,651,086 | 823,397 | 10.78x |
| 52 | `blk.7.attn_k` | 2560 x 1024 | 2,621,440 | 8,929,195 | 1,696,273 | 1,651,132 | 823,291 | 10.85x |
| 53 | `blk.7.attn_output` | 4096 x 2560 | 10,485,760 | PENDING | 5,844,812 | 5,592,124 | 2,357,551 | - |
| 54 | `blk.7.ffn_gate` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 12,701,128 | 12,066,600 | 3,972,668 | - |
| 55 | `blk.7.ffn_up` | 2560 x 9728 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 12,696,438 | 12,069,169 | 3,971,366 | - |
| 56 | `blk.7.ffn_down` | 9728 x 2560 | 24,903,680 | PENDING | 14,196,333 | 13,483,443 | 5,709,937 | - |
| | **ALL 3** | | | **53,319,770** | **8,958,303** | **8,688,595** | **3,718,139** | **14.34x** |

### Where the gemm speedup comes from (n = 3 nodes with all four stages)

| step | geo mean | min | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream to +repack -- row-parallel 64x1 layout | **5.60x** | 5.24x | 6.38x |
| +repack to +prefetch -- zicbop weight stream | **1.03x** | 1.03x | 1.03x |
| +prefetch to +vd4dots -- Andes XAndesVDot | **2.19x** | 2.01x | 2.60x |
| **total** | **12.61x** | | |
<!-- END GEMM TABLE -->

The four `upstream` cells still running are the most expensive legs in the
grid: at roughly 1 cycle per weight per token, `pristine` ffn_down is ~97M
cycles, about 8 hours of RTL. The three completed nodes already fix the shape
of the answer; the remaining four extend it, they do not change it.

## The finding: prefill and decode reach the same place by different routes

Per-stage, the same tensor (`blk.7.attn_v`), prefill measured here and decode
from the matching sweep:

| stage | gemm (prefill, 4 tok) | gemv (decode, 2 tok) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream | 8,879,897 | 4,478,183 |
| +repack | 1,695,440 (**5.24x**) | 2,145,948 (**2.09x**) |
| +prefetch | 1,651,086 (**1.03x**) | 1,387,101 (**1.55x**) |
| +vd4dots | 823,397 (**2.01x**) | -- (published 3.83x) |

The totals land close together, but almost none of it is the same work:

- **Prefill takes its win from the layout.** 5.24-6.38x at the repack stage,
  against 2.09x for decode.
- **Prefetch is nearly a no-op for prefill** (1.03x) where it is worth 1.55x
  for decode.
- **vd4dots pays about half as much** for prefill (2.01-2.60x vs 3.83x).

### Why -- both halves are visible in the source

**Upstream has no prefill kernel at all.** `GGML_TYPE_Q1_0` sets `.nrows = 1`
(`ggml-cpu.c:257`), and `ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat_one_chunk` issues one
`vec_dot` per (weight row, token) pair. So upstream cost is exactly linear in
token count, which the measurement confirms on two independent nodes:

| node | 2 tokens | 4 tokens | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| K=51 `attn_v` | 4,478,183 | 8,879,897 | 1.98x |
| K=52 `attn_k` | 4,513,768 | 8,929,195 | 1.98x |

**The repack gemm kernel amortizes every weight-side operation across the
M-tile.** Per 4 columns of weights:

| kernel | vlm mask loads | vmerge | `nds.vd4dots.vv` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv (`q1_vd4dots_x4_m2`, `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1809`) | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| gemm (`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`) | 1 | 1 | 4 |

The gemm loads one weight vector and fires four dots against it, one per token
(`q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2` reuses `%[w]` across accumulators `a0..a3`). That single
change is worth ~4x on all weight traffic, which is why the layout stage pays
so much more at prefill -- and, having removed the memory stall up front, why
there is little left for the prefetch stage to hide.

## Notes

- **Identical shapes give identical cycles.** `attn_v` and `attn_k` are both
  2560x1024 and agree to 0.003% at `prefetch` and 0.01% at `d4`; `ffn_gate` and
  `ffn_up` are both 2560x9728 and agree to 0.02%. That is the noise floor.
- **Total speedup grows with row count.** attn_q (4096 rows) reaches 17.14x
  where attn_v (1024 rows) reaches 10.78x. Upstream scales exactly 4x between
  them (8.88M -> 35.5M) but the vd4dot kernel scales only 2.52x
  (823K -> 2.07M), because per-call fixed costs -- notably the once-per-call
  activation restaging -- amortize over more 64-row tiles.
- **The prefetch stage tracks L3 residency.** 1.027x on attn_v (360 KB
  repacked, fits the 2 MB L3) against 1.053x on ffn_down (3.5 MB, does not).
  Weight reuse across the M-tile already hides the rest.
- **Cross-checks against earlier sessions.** This grid re-derived five numbers
  recorded by previous sessions, all within 1%: gemm K=51 `baseline`
  (1,695,440 vs 1,696,704), `prefetch` (1,651,086 vs 1,651,949), `d4` (823,397
  vs 818,314), gemm K=56 `prefetch` (13,483,443 vs 13,474,132) and `d4`
  (5,709,937 vs 5,683,029).

## Reproducing

```sh
bash sweep.sh --selfcheck    # gate: re-derive two published K=51 numbers
bash sweep.sh                # the prefill grid, K=50..56 x 4 variants
MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh      # the matching decode grid
bash sweep.sh --md           # regenerate the table above from the logs
```

Legs are independent, resumable, and safe to run concurrently: each hybrid run
stages into its own temp dir, and the cycle figure comes from a cycle-accurate
RTL model, so host load cannot move it.

content.text:
Answering your goal - gemm's per-stage speedup, measured the same way as gemv:

| step | **gemm (prefill)** | gemv (decode) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream -> +repack | **5.91x** | 2.13x |
| +repack -> +prefetch | **1.04x** | 1.56x |
| +prefetch -> +vd4dots | **2.37x** | 3.70x |
| **total** | **14.56x** | **12.35x** |

Written to `profiling_gemm.md`, with both full tables and a `sweep.sh` that regenerates them.

**The two sweeps reach a similar total by opposite routes.** Prefill takes almost everything from the repack layout; decode takes most of its win from prefetch and vd4dots. Both halves are grounded in source, not inferred:

- Upstream has no prefill kernel - `.nrows = 1` (`ggml-cpu.c:257`) means one `vec_dot` per (row, token). Measured linearity confirms it on three nodes: 1.98x, 1.98x, 2.02x cycles for 2x the tokens.
- The repack gemm loads one weight vector and fires four dots against it (`repack.cpp:1967-1972`), amortizing all weight traffic 4x - which also leaves prefetch nothing to hide.

**The finding I did not expect.** Decode's speedup is shape-invariant (11.74x-13.01x); prefill's is not (10.78x-20.83x). On the *smallest* node prefill gains less than decode. Splitting cost into per-call and per-tile terms across the five nodes sharing ne0=2560:

| | fixed per call | per tile | per tile per token |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv `d4` | 39,491 | 21,638 | 10,819 |
| gemm `d4` | **489,581** | 23,036 | **5,759** |

The gemm kernel is 1.88x more efficient per token in steady state but carries 12.4x the per-call fixed cost. That cost is unchanged across `baseline`/`prefetch`/`d4` (398K/441K/490K) while per-tile cost collapses 3.5x - so it is not the kernel. It is the activation quantizer: 4-token calls take the **pure scalar** `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` (`repack.cpp:51`) because its vector twin is gated on `__riscv_zvfh`, which the build disables, while 2-token calls fall through to the RVV-vectorized `quantize_row_q8_0`. At ~490K cycles it is now 59% of a small prefill node - larger than the kernel it feeds, and the clearest remaining prefill lever.

Two caveats stated plainly: `pristine` ffn_up and ffn_down at 4 tokens are still simulating (they exceeded my initial 12h ceiling; re-running now with 24h), so the gemm means are over 5 of 7 nodes. And gemv `d4` K=51 came out 5.1% above a published 2026-08-01 figure - these binaries are from 2026-08-19, so I kept the sweep internally consistent rather than blending builds.

---
name: q1-0-prefill-gemm-stage-breakdown
description: Q1_0 prefill/gemm 4-stage speedup measured 2026-08-28 (repack 6.11x / prefetch 1.04x / vd4dots 2.46x); prefill's fixed cost is a SCALAR activation quantizer worth ~490K cycles per node
metadata:
  type: project
---

Full 4-stage sweep on Bonsai-4B layer 7 (K=50..56, all 7 Q1_0 shapes),
`vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3`, both paths measured in one session from one binary set
(built 2026-08-19). Tables live in `profiling_gemm.md`; regenerate with
`bash sweep.sh --md`. See [[q1_0-wide-vlen-repack-rowparallel]].

Geo-mean per stage, n=7 nodes each:

| step | gemm (prefill, nrows=4) | gemv (decode, nrows=2) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream -> +repack | **6.11x** | 2.13x |
| +repack -> +prefetch | **1.04x** | 1.56x |
| +prefetch -> +vd4dots | **2.46x** | 3.70x |
| total | **15.64x** | 12.35x |

Same destination, opposite routes: prefill takes almost everything from the
repack layout, decode from prefetch+vd4dots. Decode is shape-invariant
(11.74-13.01x); prefill is NOT (10.78-20.83x) and gains LESS than decode on the
smallest node.

**The reason, and the next lever.** Split cost as `cycles = F + T*tiles` over
the five nodes with ne0=2560 (fit is tight, gemv residuals <1.1%):

| | fixed per call F | per tile T | per tile per token |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv d4 | 39,491 | 21,638 | 10,819 |
| gemm d4 | **489,581** | 23,036 | **5,759** |

The gemm is 1.88x better per token in steady state (M-tile sharing: one weight
vlm+vmerge feeds 4 dots, `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`) but carries 12.4x
the per-call fixed cost. F is ~constant across baseline/prefetch/d4
(398K/441K/490K) while T collapses 3.5x, so F is NOT the kernel -- it is the
activation quantize. `forward_mul_mat` (`repack.cpp:4456-4469`) sends 4-token
calls to `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` (`repack.cpp:51`), a PURE SCALAR
loop, because its vector twin is gated on `__riscv_zvfh` and build.sh sets
`-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`; 2-token calls are not a multiple of 4 so they fall
through to the RVV-vectorized `quantize_row_q8_0`
(`arch/riscv/quants.c:32`, gated only on `__riscv_v`).

At ~490K cycles that quantizer is 59% of a small prefill node (attn_v) and
12% of a large one -- now bigger than the kernel it feeds. Vectorizing it is
the clearest remaining prefill win.

Upstream has NO prefill kernel (`.nrows = 1`, `ggml-cpu.c:257`): measured
exactly linear in tokens, 1.96-2.02x for 2x tokens on all 7 nodes.

---
name: sweep-sh-grid-harness
description: sweep.sh runs the whole (build variant x MUL_MAT node) cycle grid in parallel, resumable, with an nrows gate and a --selfcheck against published numbers
metadata:
  type: project
---

`sweep.sh` in the llama.cpp root is the grid driver that `measure.sh` is not:
measure.sh does one node across a few variants, serially, to the terminal.
sweep.sh does variant x node, many legs at once, one log per leg, resumable.
Used to produce [[q1-0-prefill-gemm-stage-breakdown]].

```sh
bash sweep.sh --selfcheck    # gate: re-derive two published K=51 numbers
bash sweep.sh                # prefill grid, K=50..56 x 4 variants
MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh      # matching decode grid
bash sweep.sh --md           # regenerate the markdown tables from the logs
```

Things that are load-bearing, learned the hard way:

- **MODE picks the ggml path via the prompt, nothing else.** gemm = `--no-warmup`
  + 4-token prompt (nrows=4); gemv = the warmup pass (nrows=2). Every leg
  re-reads nrows from its own `[roi]` line and records BAD-NROWS rather than a
  number if it disagrees -- the wrong prompt measures the OTHER kernel and
  still prints a plausible cycle count.
- **Concurrency is safe.** Each hybrid run stages into its own `make_temp_dir`
  (andesim `driver/manifest.cpp`), no sockets, and the figure comes from an RTL
  model, so host load cannot move it. 22 legs at once was fine; ~2 GB and ~4
  threads per vsim, so ~16 legs saturates 64 cores.
- **Emit legs variant-major, slowest variant first.** xargs fills slots from
  the front; `pristine` is ~6x every other variant, so emitting it first makes
  the wall clock the longest single leg instead of the sum.
- **Budget 24 h per leg.** 12 h was NOT enough for `pristine` ffn_up/ffn_down
  at 4 tokens (~83M and ~96M cycles) when the grid ran 16-wide. A timed-out leg
  costs its whole wall clock and yields nothing.
- Two bash traps this hit: `local v=$1 log="...$v..."` reads an unset `v`
  (bash expands every word before performing any assignment), and an
  unrecognized flag must NOT fall through to the sweep -- it once started hours
  of simulation from a typo. Unknown flags now exit 2.

content.text:
Done. All 28 gemm legs and 28 gemv legs complete.

## gemm per-stage speedup, measured like gemv

| step | **gemm (prefill)** | gemv (decode) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream -> +repack | **6.11x** | 2.13x |
| +repack -> +prefetch | **1.04x** | 1.56x |
| +prefetch -> +vd4dots | **2.46x** | 3.70x |
| **total (geo mean, n=7)** | **15.64x** | **12.35x** |

Layer-7 aggregate for prefill: 351,619,546 -> 19,729,661 cycles = **17.82x**.

Deliverables: `profiling_gemm.md` (both full tables, verified to match the generator byte-for-byte) and `sweep.sh` (parallel, resumable, self-checking - regenerates everything with `--md`).

## What the numbers say

**Same destination, opposite routes.** Prefill takes almost its whole win from the repack layout; decode takes most of its win from prefetch and vd4dots. Both halves are grounded in source: upstream has no prefill kernel (`.nrows = 1`, `ggml-cpu.c:257`) and measures exactly linear in tokens (1.96-2.02x for 2x tokens on all 7 nodes), while the repack gemm loads one weight vector and fires four dots against it (`repack.cpp:1967-1972`).

**The unexpected part.** Decode's speedup is shape-invariant (11.74x-13.01x); prefill's is not (10.78x-20.83x), and on the *smallest* node prefill gains less than decode. Fitting `cycles = F + T*tiles` over the five nodes sharing ne0=2560:

| | fixed per call | per tile | per tile per token |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gemv `d4` | 39,491 | 21,638 | 10,819 |
| gemm `d4` | **489,581** | 23,036 | **5,759** |

The gemm is 1.88x better per token in steady state but carries 12.4x the per-call cost. That cost is flat across `baseline`/`prefetch`/`d4` (398K/441K/490K) while per-tile collapses 3.5x - so it is not the kernel. It is the activation quantizer: 4-token calls take the **pure scalar** `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` because its vector twin is gated on `__riscv_zvfh` which `build.sh` disables, while 2-token calls fall through to the RVV-vectorized `quantize_row_q8_0`. At ~490K cycles it is 59% of a small prefill node - now larger than the kernel it feeds, and the clearest remaining prefill lever.

Twelve numbers from earlier sessions were re-derived within 1% along the way; one was not (gemv `d4` K=51, 5.1% off a 2026-08-01 figure), so I kept this sweep to a single binary set rather than blending builds - noted in the document.

## Answer to your goal

gemm's per-stage speedup, measured exactly the way gemv was - all 7 layer-7 Q1_0 shapes, all 4 build stages, both paths in one session from one binary set:

| step | **gemm (prefill)** | gemv (decode) |
|---|---:|---:|
| upstream -> +repack | **6.11x** | 2.13x |
| +repack -> +prefetch | **1.04x** | 1.56x |
| +prefetch -> +vd4dots | **2.46x** | 3.70x |
| **total (geo mean)** | **15.64x** | **12.35x** |

Layer-7 aggregate for prefill: 351,619,546 -> 19,729,661 cycles = **17.82x**.

**Deliverables**
- `profiling_gemm.md` - both full tables, per-node comparison, mechanism analysis. Verified to match the generator byte-for-byte.
- `sweep.sh` - parallel, resumable grid driver with a `--selfcheck` gate; regenerates every table via `--md`, and does gemv with `MODE=gemv`.
- Two memory entries so this doesn't have to be rediscovered.

**Confidence.** Every one of the 56 legs passed the `nrows` gate, so none measured the wrong kernel. Twelve numbers from prior sessions were re-derived within 1%; identical shapes agree to 0.003-0.07%.

**The finding worth acting on.** Prefill and decode land at similar totals by opposite routes - prefill takes nearly everything from the repack layout. But prefill's speedup is *not* shape-invariant (10.78x-20.83x, versus decode's flat 11.74x-13.01x), and on the smallest node it gains less than decode. Decomposing into fixed and per-tile cost showed why: the gemm kernel is 1.88x more efficient per token in steady state, but carries a ~490K-cycle per-call constant that is identical across `baseline`/`prefetch`/`d4` - so it isn't the kernel. It is the activation quantizer, which drops to a **pure scalar** routine for 4-token calls because its vector twin is gated on `__riscv_zvfh` that the build disables, while 2-token calls get the RVV-vectorized one. That constant is 59% of a small prefill node - bigger than the kernel it feeds, and the clearest next prefill win.

One caveat on method: I ran the matching gemv sweep because the existing decode data had `baseline` at only one node and pre-F9 `d4` values, so it could not be compared stage-for-stage against F9-era gemm numbers.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Cycle sweep over the whole (build variant x MUL_MAT node) grid, in parallel.
3	#
4	# measure.sh runs ONE node across a few variants, serially, straight to the
5	# terminal. This runs the grid: every variant against every node, many legs at
6	# once, one log per leg, so a killed or timed-out leg is re-run on its own
7	# without repeating the rest. The deliverable is the table --report prints.
8	#
9	#   bash sweep.sh                      # gemm/prefill, K=50..56, all 4 variants
10	#   MODE=gemv bash sweep.sh            # the decode path instead
11	#   NODES="51 56" VARIANTS="prefetch d4" bash sweep.sh
12	#   J=4 bash sweep.sh                  # 4 legs at a time (default 8)
13	#   bash sweep.sh --report             # re-print the table, run nothing
14	#   bash sweep.sh --selfcheck          # gate: reproduce two published numbers
15	#
16	# MODE picks the ggml path by picking the prompt, which is the ONLY thing that
17	# decides it (opt_roadmap F7, "MEASUREMENT GOTCHA"):
18	#   gemv  the warmup forward pass          -> nrows=2, decode kernel
19	#   gemm  --no-warmup + a 4-token prompt   -> nrows=4, pure prefill, no gemv tail
20	# The [roi] line reports nrows, and a leg whose nrows disagrees with MODE is
21	# recorded as BAD-NROWS instead of as a number. This matters more than it
22	# looks: the wrong prompt measures the OTHER kernel and still prints a
23	# perfectly plausible cycle count, so the count alone can never catch it.
24	#
25	# Concurrency is safe: each hybrid run stages into its own make_temp_dir
26	# (andesim driver/manifest.cpp), and the cycle figure comes from a
27	# cycle-accurate RTL model, so host load cannot move it. --selfcheck proves
28	# both claims at once by running two legs together and comparing each against
29	# its published value.
30	#
31	# Slow: the RTL leg runs at a few kHz. A leg costs about 1 hour per 12M cycles,
32	# so the pristine ffn_* prefill legs are ~8 h each. Everything else is minutes.
33	set -u
34	export TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-/home/nick/tmp}
35	LLAMA=${LLAMA:-/home/nick/work/llama.cpp}
36	ANDESIM=${ANDESIM:-/home/nick/work/andesim}
37	# MODEL=4b|8b|27b picks the gguf AND the guest-RAM settings it needs. The big
38	# models do not fit the guest window mapped, so they need --no-mmap and a much
39	# larger --mem-size; getting this wrong does not error, it trap-storms.
40	#
41	# The resolved path goes in GGUF, NOT back into MODEL. MODEL arrives exported
42	# (`MODEL=27b bash sweep.sh`), so overwriting it with the path would re-export
43	# the path, and the `--leg` children xargs spawns would then resolve a
44	# DIFFERENT tag than their parent -- and so a different $OUT than the one the
45	# parent created.
46	TAG=${MODEL:-4b}
47	case "$TAG" in
48	  4b)  GGUF=$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf;  MEM=${MEM:-2000M}; MMAP=${MMAP-} ;;
49	  8b)  GGUF=$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-8B-Q1_0.gguf;  MEM=${MEM:-6G};    MMAP=${MMAP---no-mmap} ;;
50	  27b) GGUF=$LLAMA/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf; MEM=${MEM:-12G};   MMAP=${MMAP---no-mmap} ;;
51	  *)   GGUF=$TAG; MEM=${MEM:-12G}; MMAP=${MMAP---no-mmap}
52	       TAG=$(basename "$GGUF" .gguf) ;;
53	esac
54	ENGINE=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3}
55	MODE=${MODE:-gemm}
56	NODES=${NODES:-"50 51 52 53 54 55 56"}
57	VARIANTS=${VARIANTS:-"pristine baseline prefetch d4"}
58	J=${J:-8}
59	# Hybrid per-leg spawn timeout, ms. 24 h, because 12 h was NOT enough: the two
60	# largest upstream prefill legs (pristine ffn_up / ffn_down, ~83M and ~97M
61	# cycles) timed out at 12 h when the grid was running 16-wide. A timed-out leg
62	# costs its whole wall clock and yields nothing, so this is deliberately set
63	# well above the worst leg rather than close to it.
64	TIMEOUT=${TIMEOUT:-86400000}
65	# Per model AND per path: the node index K means a different tensor in a
66	# different model, so 4B and 27B results must never share a directory.
67	# 4b keeps the original unsuffixed names so the existing sweeps still resolve.
68	OUT=${OUT:-$LLAMA/sweep-$MODE$([ "$TAG" = 4b ] || echo "-$TAG")}
69	
70	case "$MODE" in
71	  gemm) PROMPT="The capital of France"; WARMUP="--no-warmup"; WANT_NROWS=4 ;;
72	  gemv) PROMPT="The capital of France is"; WARMUP="";         WANT_NROWS=2 ;;
73	  *) echo "MODE must be gemm or gemv (got '$MODE')" >&2; exit 2 ;;
74	esac
75	
76	bin_of() {  # $1 variant  $2 node -> the binary build.sh produced for that pair
77	  local suf=""; [ "$2" = 51 ] || suf="-k$2"
78	  printf '%s/bin-%s%s\n' "$LLAMA" "$1" "$suf"
79	}
80	
81	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- one leg ---
82	# Runs to completion, leaves everything in the log. Never parses; --report is
83	# the single parser, so a leg re-run and a fresh report cannot disagree.
84	run_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
85	  # Separate statements on purpose: bash expands every word of a `local` line
86	  # before it performs any of the assignments, so a log="...$v..." on the same
87	  # line would read an unset v.
88	  local v=$1 k=$2
89	  local log="$OUT/$v-k$k.log"
90	  local bin
91	  bin=$(bin_of "$v" "$k")
92	  if [ ! -x "$bin" ]; then
93	    echo "SKIP $v k=$k: no $bin (run: ROI_K=$k bash build.sh $v)" >&2
94	    return 0
95	  fi
96	  # Resume: a leg that already produced both lines is done. Anything else
97	  # (empty, truncated, timed out) is re-run.
98	  if [ -f "$log" ] && grep -q '^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" && grep -q '\[roi\] MUL_MAT' "$log"; then
99	    echo "have $v k=$k"
100	    return 0
101	  fi
102	  echo "run  $v k=$k -> $log"
103	  ( cd "$ANDESIM" && ./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux \
104	      --mem-size "$MEM" --engine "$ENGINE" --step-timeout-ms "$TIMEOUT" \
105	      "$bin" -- -m "$GGUF" $MMAP -no-cnv $WARMUP --prompt "$PROMPT" \
106	      -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 ) > "$log" 2>&1
107	  local rc=$?
108	  grep -E '\[roi\] MUL_MAT|^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" | sed "s/^/    $v k=$k: /"
109	  [ $rc -eq 0 ] || echo "    $v k=$k: exit $rc" >&2
110	}
111	
112	# --------------------------------------------------------------- reporting ---
113	# One log -> "cycles<TAB>nrows<TAB>tensor<TAB>shape", or a reason it is not a
114	# number. Kept in awk so the nrows gate and the cycle read come from the same
115	# pass over the same file.
116	read_leg() {  # $1 variant  $2 node
117	  local log="$OUT/$1-k$2.log"
118	  [ -f "$log" ] || { printf 'MISSING\t\t\t\n'; return; }
119	  # [roi] MUL_MAT #51 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [2560 x 1024] nrows=4
120	  awk -v want="$WANT_NROWS" '
121	    /\[roi\] MUL_MAT/ {
122	      for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
123	        if ($i ~ /^src0=/)   { name = substr($i, 6) }
124	        if ($i ~ /^nrows=/)  { nrows = substr($i, 7) }
125	        if ($i ~ /^\[[0-9]+$/) { ne1 = $(i+2); sub(/\]$/, "", ne1)
126	                                 shape = substr($i, 2) "x" ne1 }

content.text:
The 27B gemm grid is running - 48 legs, 12 at a time, 305 GB headroom.

**Preflight confirmed the run is valid**, which was not a given: K=48 brackets `blk.6.attn_qkv` [5120 x 10240] at `nrows=4`. qwen35's SSM layers could have built a different graph for prefill than for decode, which would have invalidated the whole node map from `profiling_data.md`; they do not, because the decode baseline is already a 2-token pass, so both fall in the same chunk.

**Two bugs caught before they burned simulator time.** The first launch exited in seconds having done nothing: `sweep.sh` reassigned the resolved `.gguf` path back into `MODEL`, and since `MODEL=27b` was *exported*, every `--leg` child inherited the path, derived a different tag, and wrote to a directory the parent never created. Twelve legs failing that way looks indistinguishable from a fast successful sweep. Fixed by resolving into a separate `GGUF` variable, plus a defensive `mkdir -p` in the leg itself. I also made `OUT` model-scoped so 27B results can never mix into the 4B directories - the node index K means a different tensor in each model.

**What you will get**, mirroring the decode tables: per-node cycles and per-stage speedup (upstream -> +repack -> +prefetch -> +vd4dots) for all 8 SSM nodes and the 4 attention-specific nodes.

**Two scope calls I made**, both following `profiling_data.md`'s own precedent:
- K=60/61/62 (the attention layer's `ffn_gate`/`ffn_up`/`ffn_down`) are the same shapes as K=53/54/55 and will be carried across rather than measured - they would need 12 new builds plus three more 17-21h legs for no new information. My 4B run showed identical shapes agree to 0.003-0.07%.
- The `baseline`/`prefetch`/`d4` legs should all land within ~5h. The 7 large `pristine` legs are a long tail, `ffn_down` alone ~21h. If measured upstream proves too slow to be useful, I can derive it as 2x the decode value - upstream is exactly linear in tokens - but I would rather measure it, so I have launched all of them.

content.text:
First results, and they validate the key assumption. Both `pristine` legs confirm the 2x token linearity holds on 27B:

| node | decode (2 tok) | prefill (4 tok) | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| K=49 `ssm_alpha` | 474,303 | 936,969 | **1.98x** |
| K=50 `ssm_beta` | 476,969 | 949,957 | **1.99x** |

Node identities also match `profiling_data.md` exactly (`blk.6.ssm_alpha` [5120 x 48], `blk.6.ssm_beta`). That means if the big upstream legs prove too slow, deriving them as 2x the decode value is now empirically backed on this model, not just on 4B.

These two are also the repack-gate failures (48 rows, `ne1 % 64 != 0`), so their `baseline`/`prefetch`/`d4` legs should come back at roughly the same ~940K - a useful negative control.
